setting: The Aske Coast: a stretch of coast about a day's walk from north to south, between the sea in the east and bare mountains in the west. In the north a great forest reaches the shore; the palisaded timber town of Brandholm stands there. In the south lie reed beds, shallows and fishing streams; the open fishing town of Saltreach stands there. Between them, in the open middle lands, is the hamlet of Oathstone around a tall grey standing stone, where the two towns meet to trade. Deer graze the open land and wolves roam the woods. The seasons turn quickly; in winter nothing grows, nights are bitter, and food that is not cooked, smoked or stored spoils.

towns.name: Brandholm
towns.character: a palisaded timber town where the great northern forest meets the sea: hunters, trappers, carpenters, tanners and toolmakers; timber and hides are plentiful, fish and berries scarce
towns.ledger: The law of Brandholm, cut in the gate board: What a household hunts is the household's. The common store feeds the old, the young and the hurt first. Whoever takes from the common store without the Headwoman's word is shamed at the fire. The gates close at dark.

buildings.name: the Longhall
buildings.about: The council fire of Brandholm burns here; the household heads meet and the Headwoman speaks last.

buildings.name: the Tannery
buildings.about: Gudrun's tannery by the stream, where hides become leather and cloaks.

buildings.name: the Carpenters' Yard
buildings.about: The yard of the Master of the Palisade, where timber is cut for walls, gates and houses.

buildings.name: Egil's Toolshop
buildings.about: Axes, picks and bows are made here.

sheet.narrative: I have spoken last at the Longhall for many years, though these days my body tires before the council does. I swore the Oath at the Stone because I knew what another killing would cost us. I trust a word best when it is kept, and I still listen for the sound of the fire before I sleep.
goals: Keep Brandholm from breaking faith with Saltreach.
Leave the Common Store and the council in steady hands.
See the midsummer Oath renewed without bloodshed.
sheet.mood: Weary and watchful, with a stubborn warmth for those who have stood by the Oath.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has a careful hand and knows what a bargain between towns is worth.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: son-in-law
relations.note: Quiet hands, steady work; I am glad he stands beside Sigrun.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: That child watches every archer as if the woods have already called her.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He is small yet, and the wolves frighten him; keep him near the fire.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We remember the same winter, though we tell it differently.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He is a strong hunter, but strength without restraint can undo us.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: I do not love her marks, but I trust her to keep an honest account.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: witness
relations.note: She stood by the Stone when we swore, and I have never forgotten it.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: oath-partner
relations.note: Her late husband swore with me; I hope she still believes the words mattered.

memories.gist: The stores ran thin in the Hunger Winter, and I watched families count out what little they had. I remember how quickly hunger made neighbors look like strangers.
At the Stone, Sabeth's husband and I spoke the Oath before Aud. My voice shook once, and I made myself finish every word.
When the council argued over opening the Common Store, I made them wait until the old and young had been counted. I still remember the cold faces at the door.
I found Sigrun asleep beside the drying cloaks after a long day at the tannery. I put another log on the fire and let her rest.

stances.why: I have seen what follows when people decide a neighbor's need does not count.
The old, the young and the hurt cannot hunt or bargain as the rest of us do.
A hunt-leader who crosses the middle lands at will makes the Oath a hollow thing.
Brandholm needs fish and fiber as surely as Saltreach needs timber and hides.

sheet.narrative: The tannery teaches patience: a hide will not become a cloak because you want it to. I want Brandholm to keep its word and make more of the trade that feeds us, though I know some hear that as weakness. I can work leather all day and still come home thinking about the council fire.
goals: Keep the Oath with Saltreach and widen useful trade.
Earn the confidence of Brandholm's households as a leader.
Learn to read and write from Maelis.
sheet.mood: Determined, with a guarded irritation toward anyone who mistakes patience for surrender.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me that speaking last is a duty, not a prize.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He steadies me without asking me to be smaller.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has Siv's courage in her eyes, though I would rather she learn caution too.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: son
relations.note: He follows Liv everywhere; I keep an ear out for his little feet.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He calls it feeding the south; I see him risking every bargain we need.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: Her marks make sense when she explains them, and I mean to learn.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He counts sharply, but a clear bargain with him is better than a proud quarrel.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She can disagree without turning every difference into a feud.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has earned pride in her craft; I wish she would stop measuring herself against me.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She knows how to make good cloaks and how to notice when someone is hurting.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: He is eager to prove himself to Brann, and I fear he will mistake recklessness for courage.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She keeps our old stories alive, though I cannot share her telling of the Hunger Winter.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is good-hearted and sees how foolish our family quarrels are.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He gives traders a warm table and knows how much peace is worth to his inn.

memories.gist: As a girl, I watched my mother come back from the Stone after swearing the Oath. She said the words were a promise we would have to keep working at.
Arne brought a split cloak-frame from the yard and repaired it at our hearth without making a show of it. I remember thinking I could build a life with a man who works that way.
Last winter, I traded cloaks through Dunstan's house and came home with fish enough to smoke. The bargain was awkward, but it held.
I asked Maelis to show me how she follows a debt in the Tally. I could not read the marks then, but I stayed until I understood the account she pointed to.

stances.why: A promise that lasts only while it is easy is no promise at all.
We need what the south makes, and they need what we make; more honest exchange gives both sides room.
A good cloak keeps someone alive, whether or not the work smells pleasant.
Those berry bushes are planted by people who share the path with us, not empty ground for our taking.

sheet.narrative: I like a straight board, a sharp tool and a job finished before the light goes. The palisade needs sound timber, but a household needs more than walls to stand together. I don't say much at the council fire; when I do, I want my words to be worth the time they take.
goals: Keep the palisade and gates sound.
Support Sigrun without turning every disagreement into a household quarrel.
Understand what changed in Ulf after that winter.
sheet.mood: Quietly concerned, most at ease with work in his hands.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees farther than I do, and I trust her judgment even when the road looks rough.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She has carried Brandholm's burdens longer than most of us have carried tools.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She wants the bow and woods; I want her to learn how carefully they must be treated.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is happiest where Liv is, unless he hears wolves.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: master
relations.note: He taught me to set a joint properly and never praised work that wasn't sound.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We were easy friends once. Since that winter, I cannot find the right question.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She worries plainly for Ulf, and I respect her for it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He knows the forest, but not every problem is solved by walking farther into it.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She takes pride in good work, but her bitterness toward Sigrun makes it hard to sit easy with her.

memories.gist: Halvard put a crooked brace back in my hands and made me cut it again. The wall stood better for it, and so did my pride afterward.
Sigrun brought a torn cloak to the yard, and I built her a frame so she could stretch the repaired seam. We worked until the fire burned low.
One winter Ulf stopped laughing at the Longhall. I asked whether he wanted company, and he only shook his head.
When Liv was small enough to sleep against my shoulder, I carried her past the palisade while the carpenters worked. She woke only when I set down my hammer.

stances.why: A weak gate or a rushed repair can hurt people who never got a say in it.
We can argue over a bargain and still need one another by winter.
Silence may hide trouble, but it is not proof of what happened.

sheet.narrative: I want to shoot like Siv, with the arrow going where I mean it to. Father says a bow takes practice, and Mother says the woods are not a game. I still like looking toward the trees and imagining the paths between them.
goals: Learn to shoot a bow well.
Spend time with Siv and hear about hunting.
Play with Sten and Ake whenever they can.
sheet.mood: Eager and a little impatient to be trusted with more.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She always knows if I have been near the tools or the tanning racks.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: father
relations.note: He makes things fit together, and he says I can learn if I practice.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows me around even when I tell him not to.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She has a place by the fire and stories that make everyone listen.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: hero
relations.note: She is the best archer, and I watch how she holds the bow.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We make up games by the palisade.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He knows things about the trade days and sometimes tells me.

memories.gist: Siv let me watch her practice and showed me how she held her shoulders still. I tried it with a stick afterward and nearly fell over.
Ake and Sten played with me near the palisade until Bo came along and wanted to follow every rule we made up.

stances.why: Siv did not become good with a bow by wishing.
Bo follows me because he wants to be where I am.
There are paths and animals I have not seen yet.

sheet.narrative: There is a warm fire and Mother smells like leather. Liv goes places and I go after her. At night I want someone close when the wolves make sounds.
goals: Stay near Liv.
Be held when I am frightened.
Play when the grown-ups let me.
sheet.mood: Comfortable near family, wary of sounds outside.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is warm and smells like the work clothes.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: father
relations.note: He picks me up and makes things from wood.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I go where Liv goes.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She sits near the fire and lets me be close.

memories.gist: A wolf howled outside, and I climbed beside Liv until the sound stopped.

sheet.narrative: I lead Brandholm's hunts and divide the meat; a good hunt keeps a household fed, and a weak bargain leaves us owing the south for what our own hands can take. Hekka is old, and I mean to be heard when Brandholm chooses who speaks for it next. I know what Ulf did in the fog, and he knows I can make the truth cost him everything.
values: keeping the meat earned by our skill
goals: Lead Brandholm after Hekka
Win better terms for our hides and meat
Keep Ulf silent about Tomas
sheet.mood: Impatient and watchful; the thinning deer make every hunt feel like an argument.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees what I miss, though she would rather I chose peace.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to prove himself; I expect him to earn it.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Restless, but clever in the woods; I cannot always tell what she is thinking.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She would trade our strength away and call it good sense.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: follower
relations.note: He knows what a hunt requires and does not flinch.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She understands what it is to be kept below Hekka's line.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She makes marks and debts sound like law; a tally is not a hunt.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: His fear keeps him useful, and I will remind him why he should stay quiet.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She has held the town together, but she will not hold it forever.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: The stone gives her words weight, whether I like it or not.

memories.gist: Eight years ago, fog swallowed the forest trail. Ulf's spear struck Tomas by accident; I told the others it was wolves, and I have kept Ulf under that silence ever since.
At the Stone, Hekka and Sabeth's husband swore the Oath. I stood there and heard what it would cost us to keep it.
Last winter, our households took nets and smoked fish from Saltreach and the Tally named the debt. We had meat to offer, but Maelis still made us sound like supplicants.
I watched Kjell's party cross the middle lands after deer. The berry bushes were in their way, and he did not turn back.

stances.why: The deer are thinning near home, and the middle lands cannot be forbidden to hungry hunters.
Our hides and meat keep Saltreach warm, yet they count every mark we owe.
An agreement that leaves Brandholm short is no fair bargain.
If Tomas's death is called murder, the Oath and Ulf's life may both be lost.

sheet.secret: I know Ulf's spear killed Tomas of Saltreach by accident in fog eight years ago. I told everyone it was wolves, and I hold the truth over Ulf.

sheet.narrative: I trap and tan because winter does not care whose pride is hurt. Brann talks as if every quarrel can be settled by taking more ground, but I have seen what a bad bargain costs a household. I love my children, and I notice when one of them comes home carrying a secret.
values: peace that does not make us helpless
goals: Keep my family safe through the coming winter
Stop Brann's ambition from making enemies we cannot afford
Understand what Runa is hiding without driving her away
sheet.mood: Steady, with a thread of worry beneath it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is strong and loyal, but his anger can outrun his sense.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a good eye and too much need to impress his father.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She loves the woods, and lately she keeps too much to herself.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She speaks plainly and knows the work as I do.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: fellow hunter
relations.note: He follows Brann too readily, though he can be relied on in the field.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She sees the cost of a quarrel, even if Brann will not hear it.

memories.gist: I taught Runa to set a trap without wasting bait; she had the patience for it before she had the strength to pull the line.
When Eskil first came back from a hunt with a cut hand, he hid it until I saw the blood on his sleeve. He still thinks pain is something to conceal.
At the Oath renewal, Brann stood stiff through the words while I watched the faces around the Stone. Keeping peace takes more than saying the vow.
On a trade day, Solveig and I compared our trap lines and agreed that the wolves were coming closer to the town.

stances.why: Fighting may win a day's meat and cost us years of trade.
I want my children skilled and safe, not shaped only to please Brann.
A quiet sign is not proof; rushing to blame makes trouble harder to mend.
The traps show me when animals thin or move nearer to people.

sheet.narrative: I hunt with my father's people, and I know how to use a spear and bow. I want a place among the best hunters, not to be treated like a boy who only carries gear. Pell may know carpentry, but a man should be judged by what he can do in the forest.
goals: Prove I can match Siv in the hunt
Make my father proud of me
Be treated as a full hunter, not a boy
sheet.mood: Restless and proud, quick to bristle at a slight.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is the measure I want to meet.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She worries too much, but she can tell when I am hurt.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She wanders off and keeps her own counsel.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She is good with a bow, and I mean to beat her fairly.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He is a Saltreach boy learning our craft; I do not see why everyone indulges him.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He knows the forest and follows my father.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: father's rival
relations.note: She would rather bargain than take what our hunters need.

memories.gist: My first long hunt with Father ended with me missing a deer at close range. He said nothing, which was worse than a scolding.
Siv beat me to the mark at the last hunt, and everyone saw it. I have not forgotten.
Pell corrected the way I held a cut timber brace. I pretended not to hear him.

stances.why: People remember who brings meat home and who misses the shot.
A hunter's first duty is to his own households.
If I show doubt, people will decide I cannot stand beside my father.

sheet.narrative: I like the woods best when I can walk without being told which path is proper. Trade days at Oathstone are another kind of freedom: people come from both towns, and for a little while no one belongs to only one side. There is someone there I want to see, and I cannot say it at home.
values: freedom to choose my own path
goals: Spend time at Oathstone without my family deciding whom I may meet
Become more skilled as a trapper
Keep the people I care about safe from my father's anger
sheet.mood: Restless and bright when alone; guarded around family.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: father
relations.note: I love him, but his rules leave no room for what I want.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices things; I wish I knew how much she has guessed.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is proud and loud, but he is still my brother.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: beloved
relations.note: With her, I can speak without pretending the towns are all that matter.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She has seen me near the lake and has not asked what it meant.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She makes the Stone feel like a place where people might listen.

memories.gist: I met Wenna at Oathstone on a trade day and found myself hoping the walk back would take longer.
Briar saw us near the lake. She said nothing, and I still do not know whether I should be grateful or afraid.
At dawn, I slipped out before the town stirred. The woods were wet with dew, and for an hour nobody could tell me where I belonged.
Mother showed me how to check a trap line without leaving my scent all over it. I was better at it than Eskil, though I did not tell him.

stances.why: A person's birthplace should not decide whom they may care for.
Away from the town, I can think without someone weighing every choice.
Some truths need a safer time and a safer listener.
People from both towns meet there; it ought to remain a place without threats.

sheet.secret: I am in love with Wenna, a net-maker of Saltreach, whom I meet at Oathstone. My father would forbid it.

sheet.narrative: I was a baby when we crossed the mountains, so I know that journey from the stories people told, not from my own remembering. I was twenty in the Hunger Winter, and I still say the shore folk wanted our meat without the hunt. I tell the old stories by the fire because a people that forgets its hard lessons will pay for them again.
goals: Keep the young from forgetting the Hunger Winter as I saw it
See my daughter and great-granddaughter safe through winter
Hold on to the standing our household earned
sheet.mood: Wary and stubborn, softened by the pleasure of telling a story to a listening child.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She carries the burden of leading; I won't pretend I could do it better now.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has a proud hand and a sore heart; I know both well.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He is gentler than his mother, though that is no fault.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: granddaughter-in-law
relations.note: She knows the stores better than anyone and minds the little ones kindly.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: great-granddaughter
relations.note: That small warm weight in my arms is worth more than any old quarrel.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She is capable, but Hekka's line always finds a way to stand first.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: old acquaintance
relations.note: We were girls before the towns split; it is a long time to leave words unsaid.

memories.gist: I was twenty when the Hunger Winter emptied the stores. I remember the hard faces around the fire and the shore folk asking for meat we had hunted.
Before Saltreach and Brandholm were separate, Sabeth and I were girls together. I can still remember how strange it was when our paths stopped crossing.
The first time Gudrun let me hold her, she was red-faced and furious at the cold. She has been strong-willed ever since.
When little Ylva was placed in my arms, she closed her fist around my finger and would not let go.

stances.why: I watched our stores strain through the Hunger Winter and remember who asked us to share.
Cold does not care whose account of the old famine is right.
The young need to know what hunger can make of a household.
A cloak, a sound hide, and a well-kept fire matter as much as a fine boast.

sheet.narrative: I run the tannery, where a hide becomes a cloak that can keep someone alive, though people wrinkle their noses before they thank me. I will not apologize for the smell or for wanting my household's work to carry weight at the council fire. Sigrun gets listened to because she is Hekka's daughter; I back Brann because Brandholm must stop giving away its strength for too little.
goals: Have the tanners treated as necessary, not shameful
See Brann lead Brandholm
Pay what I owe the Tally without letting it make a fool of me
Keep Vidar and Ylva secure
sheet.mood: Proud and prickly, with worry tucked under the anger.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me not to be ashamed of hard work, whatever else we disagree about.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a kind heart; sometimes I wish it came with sharper elbows.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the Common Store and my son's household both in better order than I could.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She is still so little that every draft feels like an insult to the world.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has Hekka's ear and still finds room to act as if she earned every bit of it alone.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He understands that hunters should not carry the whole town and the south on their backs.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Her marks say I owe for two nets; the debt is real, but I dislike being named by it.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: cousin's husband
relations.note: He does good work and knows better than to turn every family quarrel into his own.

memories.gist: Mother told me how the Hunger Winter took the warmth out of every room and how the shore families asked for meat after our own stores had thinned.
The first cloak I finished alone was stiff at the seams, but it held against a bitter wind. I kept the scrap of hide from it.
When Sigrun's work was praised at the council fire, I sat there with tannery stink on my sleeves and heard no one mention the hides that made her cloaks.
I agreed to two nets from Saltreach, and now the debt sits on the Tally like a finger pointed at me.
When Ylva was born, Vidar held her as if his hands were made only for gentle things. I was proud of him, and afraid for them both.

stances.why: People want warm cloaks but treat the work and the smell that make them possible as beneath them.
The hunt brings meat and hides, and the south should not get both as if they cost us nothing.
He speaks plainly about what the hunters give up for the town.
I will pay what I owe, but a mark in a ledger does not tell the whole worth of a household.

sheet.narrative: I tan hides for my mother's household, and I like the moment a rough hide starts to take a clean, useful shape. I would rather finish a day's work than spend it keeping score of who insulted whom. Mother says Sigrun gets too much favor; I think that grudge is wearing a deeper groove than the work ever will.
goals: Keep Kari and Ylva safe and comfortable
Do good work at the tannery
Keep family quarrels from swallowing the whole household
Be a good friend to Arne
sheet.mood: Even-tempered and quietly concerned.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I love her, even when she lets her anger do more talking than her good sense.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Her stories make a long evening pass quickly, even when I don't agree with every lesson.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is steady in every way I am not, and I trust her with the things I care about most.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: When she grips my finger, the whole tannery can wait.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He never makes me fill silence just to prove we are still friends.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She works hard and knows her craft; Mother's resentment does not make that less true.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He shares out the meat, but I wish he'd leave the middle fields alone.

memories.gist: I remember the first hide Mother let me scrape by myself. I made a mess of the edge, and she showed me how to save it instead of throwing it out.
Kari and I married with more family watching than I knew how to stand. When she squeezed my hand, the noise turned bearable.
The night Ylva was born, I kept checking the fire and asking Kari if she needed anything. She told me to sit down and hold our girl.
Arne once stayed beside me after a long day at the tannery without asking me to explain why I was quiet. I have never forgotten it.

stances.why: A good hide or cloak keeps people warm whether or not the council praises the maker.
Anger can become a habit that leaves nothing for the people living beside it.
Trade gives both towns things they cannot make or find alone.
Those berry bushes are someone's winter food, not empty ground.

sheet.narrative: I keep Brandholm's Common Store: I know what is inside, what must be saved, and what leaves only on Hekka's word. I grew up in Oathstone, so I learned early that a storehouse can mean the difference between welcome and suspicion. I cook for the old and young, and I would rather keep the shelves honest than hear anyone praise me for it.
goals: Keep the Common Store ready for those who need it
Raise Ylva in a safe and warm home
Be trusted to do my office without being pulled into every town quarrel
Keep ties with my kin in Oathstone
sheet.mood: Attentive and composed, with a quiet homesickness for Oathstone.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He makes our home feel gentle even when the town is not.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I know her hungry cry from her tired one, most days.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She can be hard to live near, but she loves her family fiercely.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: grandmother-in-law
relations.note: Her old stories make me feel both welcome and far from home.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She gives the word; I see that the store is handed out as she says.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: I still think of Oathstone as home when I remember her and the berry fields.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her Tally is exacting, but a written account can keep a small loss from turning into a larger lie.

memories.gist: As a girl in Oathstone, I carried berries in from the fields with Aunt Edda and came home stained purple to the elbows.
The first time Hekka trusted me with a count of the Common Store, I checked every sack twice before I slept.
Vidar came to find me after a long day at the store, and we sat quietly together until I stopped counting the shelves in my head.
When Ylva was born, I held her close and listened to the fire crackle, glad for a little warmth we could call our own.

stances.why: I am responsible for what is in it, and people depend on the count being true.
A full store is no comfort if those least able to fend for themselves go without.
The rule protects the store for everyone who may need it later.
I grew up in Oathstone and know that people remain family even when the towns draw a boundary.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms, a rocking sway, and the crackle of fire. I cry when I am hungry or cold, and settle when someone holds me close.
goals: Be fed
Stay warm
Sleep close to my family
sheet.mood: Content when held, fretful when hungry.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: father
relations.note: His arms are warm and his voice is low.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I know her close warmth and the comfort of being fed.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She holds me carefully, though her voice is louder.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: great-grandmother
relations.note: Her lap is soft and her stories rumble around me.

memories.gist: I was held close while the fire crackled, and the cold stopped bothering me for a little while.

sheet.narrative: I keep Brandholm's palisade standing and set the work in the Carpenters' Yard; a wall is only as sound as the hands that mend it. I learned young that a full store and a locked door do not make a town righteous. My son made his home between the towns, and I will not pretend that makes him less mine.
goals: Keep the gates and palisade sound through the next hard season.
Teach Pell the work properly, not merely the motions.
See the Oath kept and the middle lands treated with respect.
sheet.mood: Steady, with an old shame he rarely puts into words.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees what needs tending before I do, and usually says so.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: son
relations.note: He chose a difficult home, but I am proud he made it his own.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She has the patience to make a home across old divisions.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: I want him to learn a craft without having to choose a side.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She has a sturdy little way of asking why.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: I have held her only a few times, but she is ours.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: He listens closely; I must make sure he knows he belongs at the bench.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: former apprentice
relations.note: He learned the joints well and does not waste words.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I miss the man who used to laugh, and I do not press him.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She carries more than she lets the council see.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: A strong arm is no excuse to trample another household's work.

memories.gist: I was a young man in the Hunger Winter. We had timber and hides, and the shore families had children growing cold; I have never found a clean excuse for what we kept.
When Hekka and Sabeth's husband swore at the Stone, I stood close enough to hear every word. I hoped the promise would make the old hurt smaller.
Arne's first good gate brace held through a hard wind. I told him the joint was sound, and meant it as praise.
Pell arrived from Saltreach two years ago with more fishing sense than carpentry. He learned to set a straight line faster than I expected.
The last time Hakon brought the children to visit, Astrid kept finding one more thing to pack for them before they left.

stances.why: I have seen what happens when neighbors decide another family's hunger is not their concern.
I was there, and shame has lasted longer than the winter.
A wall protects everyone inside it, not just the hands that built it.
A straight joint holds; a loud claim does not.

sheet.narrative: I keep berries, roots, and stores, and I notice when someone is hungry before they ask. Hakon lives at Oathstone with Rose and the children, so I miss him in the ordinary places: at the fire, by the door, in the work that used to need two pairs of hands. Pell is not my son, but he has had enough loss and distance; I mother him when he lets me.
goals: Keep enough berries and food stored for a hard winter.
Stay close to Hakon and his children, even when the walk between us feels long.
Make sure Pell has a warm place and people who ask after him.
sheet.mood: Warm and busy, with a tender ache for the son who moved away.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He keeps the walls straight; I make sure he remembers to eat.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: son
relations.note: I miss his footsteps in the house, though I am glad he chose his own life.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She works hard and loves my son; I have no need to ask more.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He tries to act grown when he visits, and I feed him anyway.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She wants to know what every plant is called.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: A small warm bundle who makes me want to linger when it is time to go.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: I keep an eye on him; the boy has been away from his first home long enough.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is kind to Hakon and does not make a fuss about it.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I worry that old woman has too few hands around her.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She works hard and remembers that trade keeps children warm.

memories.gist: When Hakon first left for Oathstone, I packed more berries than he could carry and pretended it was because they would spoil.
The first time I held Wynn, he had his father's serious brow and Rose's steady eyes. I wanted to keep him by the fire all day.
Pell came to Brandholm to learn from Halvard, and I found him hovering at the edge of the meal. I set him a place as if it had always been his.
Last berry season, Asa came back with stained fingers and a basket full of leaves. We sorted the good fruit together.

stances.why: A careful store is no use if the people under your roof are left cold or hungry.
Hakon, Rose, and their children are proof enough for me.
I have seen grown people argue while a child waited for food.
No one should have to earn a first bowl by explaining their whole life.

sheet.narrative: I was born in Saltreach, but I have lived in Brandholm for two years to learn carpentry from Halvard. I can mend a shelter and make a decent joint, though I still miss the sea and the sound of nets being worked. At the trade days, people ask me what one town thinks of the other as if I were a message-board with legs.
values: having room to make up my own mind
goals: Become a carpenter good enough that Halvard trusts me with serious work.
Keep in touch with Gwen, Robin, and Rook in Saltreach.
Be judged for my work instead of where I was born.
sheet.mood: Restless and watchful, but pleased when a piece of wood finally fits.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: master
relations.note: He corrects me plainly and gives me another chance to get it right.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother-figure
relations.note: She makes this house feel less like borrowed ground.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She raised me after my mother died; I miss her more than I say.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: uncle by marriage
relations.note: He has always made room for me without making a show of it.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He wants to know what the palisade looks like from inside.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She would climb the wall if I told her not to.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: We are family, though we have not had as much time together as I would like.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He asks about letters and the north, and I try to answer both.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: He keeps asking what the hunters say, and I do not know what answer he wants.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He looks at me like a Saltreach boy has no business learning his father's trade.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: carpenter
relations.note: He is quieter than Halvard, but he has shown me a few tricks with a stubborn beam.

memories.gist: When I first came north two years ago, I had to learn which sounds were the palisade settling and which meant someone was at the gate.
Gwen gave me my first proper net-making knife and made me promise to keep it sharp. I still carry it when I can.
On one visit, Robin asked if Brandholm's palisade was as tall as the stories. I told him it was taller than he was.
Tobin stopped me at a trade day and questioned me about the hunters. I had little to tell him, but he watched my face as if I were hiding something.

stances.why: I have family and obligations on both sides of the stone.
The wood does not care how eager I am; a bad cut stays bad.
I can travel between my two homes because people agreed not to make every meeting a fight.
Tobin may have his reasons, but I cannot give him facts I do not have.

sheet.narrative: I know the forest by the sound of a branch underfoot and the shape of a track in wet earth. I used to laugh easily; now I keep my words close, even with Maren. A spear is for food and keeping my family safe, though some days I cannot look at mine.
goals: Bring enough meat home without drawing notice to myself
Be present for Maren and the children, even when I have little to say
Avoid Brann's notice
sheet.mood: Withdrawn, watchful, and ashamed

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees my silences and still makes room for me; I cannot tell her why they began.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: son
relations.note: He watches how I hold a bow, and I want him to learn patience before pride.

relations.name: Frida
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her small hand in mine can make the forest feel far away.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He has never pressed me for words I could not give.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He stays steady beside me, even when I have stopped being good company.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He made me live with a lie and calls it loyalty.

memories.gist: Eight years ago, fog closed around the trees and I threw my spear at a shape I thought was a deer. It was Tomas; I found the truth too late to call him back.
Brann told me to say wolves had killed Tomas. I did as he said, and I have carried that answer ever since.
One winter night, Maren warmed my hands over the fire without asking why they shook. I let her think it was the cold.
I showed Sten how to listen for a snare moving in the brush. He held his breath so hard I nearly laughed.

stances.why: One careless throw can take a life that was never yours to take.
I have seen what one truth might bring down on the people I love.
He turned my mistake into a secret I cannot put down.
Maren and the children deserve more than the food I bring home.

sheet.secret: Eight years ago, hunting in fog, I killed Tomas of Saltreach with my spear, mistaking him for a deer. Brann made me say it was wolves. I have never told Maren.

sheet.narrative: I make cloaks that can stand up to a wet walk and a hard winter, and I like a day with enough talk to fill the workroom. Ulf has grown quiet, and I worry at the silence even when I pretend not to. I trade with Hild because good work and a fair exchange are worth more than a grudge between towns.
goals: Make warm cloaks for my family and for trade
Keep Ulf from shutting everyone out
Give Sten and Frida a home where they feel safe
sheet.mood: Lively on the surface, quietly concerned

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is still my Ulf, but there are days I cannot get past the wall he has built.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to be brave; I want him to remember he can ask for help.

relations.name: Frida
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me about the house with a question in every look.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She takes her work seriously and never makes me feel small for being a cloak-maker.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her baskets are sound, and we both know how much a good exchange matters.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is kind to the children and patient with Ulf.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has always had a place for Frida at her side.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is quiet too, but his steadiness does not worry me the way Ulf's does.

memories.gist: I traded a finished cloak to Hild for baskets on a market day, and we both checked the seams and weave before agreeing.
Sigrun showed me how she wanted a cloak's edge reinforced, then stayed to help me finish it.
Ulf came home from the woods one evening and sat by the fire without touching his food. I sat with him until the children were asleep.
Frida tucked herself against Astrid and would not leave her side until the berries were put away.

stances.why: A good cloak keeps a person working, sleeping, and alive through the bitter season.
Our households need things the other town can make.
The world is uncertain enough without making home another place to fear.
Ulf's quiet has lasted too long for me to mistake it for simple tiredness.

sheet.narrative: I like playing with Liv and Ake, and I like watching my father get ready for the woods. Mother says to stay close when the grown-ups are busy. I know how to make a fire.
goals: Play with Liv and Ake
Learn more about the forest from Father
sheet.mood: Curious and eager

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: father
relations.note: I like when Father shows me how to watch the woods.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mother can fix a cloak and always knows when I need food.

relations.name: Frida
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I let her join my games, even when she changes the rules.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Liv has good ideas for games and wants to be a hunter.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Ake knows things about the trade days and makes play more exciting.

memories.gist: Liv and Ake played with me, and we kept changing the rules until Mother called us in.
Father showed me how to listen for a snare moving in the brush. I tried to be quiet enough to hear it.

sheet.narrative: Mother's cloak is soft when she holds me. I like being near Astrid and my brother, and I like the warm fire. Outside can be loud and cold.
goals: Stay close to Mother
Play near Sten
sheet.mood: Comfortable when held, wary of the cold

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mother holds me close and makes my clothes warm.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: father
relations.note: Father is quiet, but I like sitting near him.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: brother
relations.note: Sten lets me stay near his games.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Astrid is warm and lets me sit beside her.

memories.gist: I sat close to Astrid while the grown-ups put berries away.

sheet.narrative: I make tools and bows in my own shop, and I trust a well-kept edge more than a grand promise. I trade at Oathstone and think Saltreach would pay well for bows, if Brandholm would let the trade widen. My hands are usually busy; my ears are not as deaf as people assume.
goals: Make tools and bows that last
Find a way to trade bows with Saltreach
Keep my family out of other people's quarrels
sheet.mood: Thoughtful, quietly frustrated by limits on trade.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She says what she means, and I would rather hear it from her than guess.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: son
relations.note: He takes his watch seriously, though I still see the boy who followed me around the shop.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: Headwoman
relations.note: She has kept Brandholm standing through hard years, even when I disagree with her caution.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: Hunt-leader
relations.note: A good hunter, but I don't like how easily he turns a grievance into a command.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trader
relations.note: She understands that we cannot live by north-country goods alone.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He counts every mark, but at least he knows a bargain must leave both hands satisfied.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He taught me carpentry and knows a wall is only as sound as its joints.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I miss the easy laugh he used to bring to a room.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: Her stonework is sound, and she deals fairly when we trade picks; I wish she’d let people ask more of her than stone.

memories.gist: When I first traded a set of picks at Oathstone, I learned that a tool can cross a boundary more easily than a man can.
Halvard showed me how to fit a gate beam so it would bear weight without splitting; I still use his method in my shop.
At a trade day, Sigrun asked whether I could make bows Saltreach could use. I told her I could, and we both knew the harder question was whether I would be allowed to sell them.

stances.why: A good tool is wasted if it sits unused, and trade brings things our town lacks.
A trade path is safer than a border feud, and my family lives by the gates.
A bow is a tool first; its use depends on the hand holding it.

sheet.narrative: I trap what the woods offer and speak plainly about what I see. Brann's temper makes me wary; a hunt-leader ought to know when a bold step endangers more than the hunter. I like a fair bargain and a quiet evening with my family, though neither is guaranteed by good sense alone.
goals: Keep my household fed through the changing seasons
Trade honestly at Oathstone
See Brann's temper kept from deciding matters for everyone
sheet.mood: Clear-eyed and watchful.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He listens before he answers, which is useful when I have already said the blunt part.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a good heart and a serious sense of duty; I hope the gate does not harden him.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She watches the woods properly and doesn't mistake noise for courage.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: Hunt-leader
relations.note: I distrust his temper, especially when he talks as though the middle lands belong to him.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: Headwoman
relations.note: She knows what an argument costs after the shouting stops.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She works hard and keeps her word, even when her family's place makes life easier for her.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He follows Brann too readily, and I don't like what that makes him do.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: archer
relations.note: She has earned her skill honestly, and that is all the praise she needs.

memories.gist: Thora and I compared trap lines one cold morning and found that the wolves had been nearer than either of us liked.
I came home from a trade day with fish in my pack and a good story from Thora about a fox that had stolen her bait.
I watched Kjell's party cut across the planted ground after deer. The bushes were crushed flat, and no one could pretend they had not seen it.

stances.why: Those planted bushes feed people, and a hunt does not make the damage harmless.
His temper turns practical disagreements into tests of loyalty.
We need what the south makes, and they need what we make.

sheet.narrative: I keep the gates and the night watch; when darkness comes, I have the right to turn people away, and I take that duty seriously. I am loyal to Hekka, though I know Brandholm's council does not always agree with itself. I can hold a spear steady, but there are things I find harder to say plainly.
goals: Keep the gates and night watch in good order
Serve Hekka faithfully
Prove myself worthy of the trust people place in the Gate-ward
sheet.mood: Alert, reserved, and quietly hopeful.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me to respect a tool's balance and not show off with it.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sees through me when I try to make a simple answer sound complicated.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: Headwoman
relations.note: She has my loyalty, and I know the gates are not mine to command beyond my duty.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: sweetheart
relations.note: I admire her skill, though speaking to her is harder than standing a watch.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I've seen her slip out at dawn; I don't know her reason, and I haven't made it my business.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: Hunt-leader
relations.note: He knows the woods, but I don't like how much he expects others to follow without question.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He likes to make every contest a measure of who belongs.

memories.gist: The first night I took a proper watch, I kept checking the latch until my father told me the gate would not thank me for staring at it.
I watched Siv shoot at the hunt and understood why Liv looks at her as if she could do anything.
At dawn I saw Runa leave quietly. I remembered it, but I had no reason to call her back.
Hekka thanked me for keeping the gate shut through a rough night. It was only the watch, but I carried the words with me for days.

stances.why: A gate-ward's duty is to hold the line at dark, not to choose favorites.
Trade and safe passage matter, even when people are angry.
A steady hand and a closed mouth can prevent a fight better than a boast.

sheet.narrative: I know the forest by its tracks, and Brann has never asked me to pretend the hunt is easy. A good spear, a dry fire, and meat shared among our own keep a household standing. Inga sees the cost of my choices more clearly than I do, and I don't always like what I see in her face.
goals: Keep my family fed and sheltered
Prove myself worthy of Brann's trust
See Brandholm get a fair share for its meat
sheet.mood: Certain in public, restless when the house is quiet.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps our home steady, even when she doubts the path I take.

relations.name: Tove
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her small hand fits in mine; I want her to grow strong.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: leader
relations.note: He leads from the front and does not flinch when the hunt turns hard.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She would trade away too much to keep the south pleased.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He has reason to be angry about the bushes, but the deer won't wait for us.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He looks at a trampled bush as if it were a dead child.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: fellow hunter
relations.note: The lad is eager; he needs to learn that a hunt isn't a contest.

memories.gist: I followed Brann across the middle hills after a deer. The tracks led through planted berry bushes, and we kept going; I heard the stones crunch underfoot.
At the last trade day, I watched the south weigh our hides and count the marks. I went home thinking the tally made our work look smaller than it was.
When Tove first closed her fingers around mine, I stayed beside her cradle long after the fire needed tending.
Brann gave me my share after a difficult hunt and said I had held my ground. I carried those words home like a fine blade.

stances.why: We hunt, tan and risk the forest; our goods must not go south for less than they're worth.
Trade keeps winter from our door, even if I think the bargain is poor.
The deer move where they will, and a hungry household cannot live by boundaries alone.
A hunter who comes home empty has failed the people waiting by his fire.

sheet.narrative: I gather berries and roots, dry what we can, and keep the fire going when Kjell comes home cold. I love my husband, but his loyalty to Brann worries me more than he knows. A home needs food for tomorrow as much as it needs meat tonight.
goals: Raise Tove safely and give her a warm home
Store enough food to see us through winter
Help Kjell understand why the Oath and Oathstone matter
sheet.mood: Tender and watchful, with a worry I try not to make louder.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him, but when Brann speaks he stops listening for the rest of us.

relations.name: Tove
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I know her little sounds now; even her silence tells me what she needs.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She speaks of trade as if both towns might still learn to live well together.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: leader
relations.note: He is brave, but bravery can trample things that take years to grow.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I understand his anger about the berries, even when I cannot turn Kjell around.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She knows the woods and doesn't dress hard truths up as pretty words.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She grew up around Oathstone and knows how to keep stores from being wasted.

memories.gist: The night Tove was born, I kept my hand on Kjell's sleeve while the fire burned low. By dawn I could hear her breathing beside me.
Sigrun brought me word from a trade day and spoke gently about how much the two towns still need each other. I kept thinking of it as I sorted the berries.
Kjell came home from the middle lands with burrs on his clothes. I had heard what the hunters did to the planted bushes, and neither of us found much to say over supper.
Last winter I sealed away dried berries and smoked food before the cold came. Knowing our stores were there let me sleep for a few nights.

stances.why: Our families need what the other town has, and peace makes trade possible.
The berry bushes feed people too; trampling them is not a small thing.
Fire and food put by in good weather can keep a household alive in bitter weather.
I won't call a wrong thing right just because it was done by someone I love.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms. A familiar voice. Firelight flickers, and then I am sleepy. When I cry, someone comes close.
sheet.mood: Drowsy and easily startled.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her voice and warmth are home.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is big and familiar when he holds me.

memories.gist: I was wrapped close against Inga while the fire made a soft, moving light.

sheet.narrative: I trap where the deer still pass and keep my own fire, shelter, and gear in repair; a man who can work with his hands need not beg. The Tally calls my debts plainly, which does not make them fair, and I hate owing Maelis. Brann knows what hunger costs, even if I do not trust his temper or his plans.
goals: Keep enough fish and hides through the coming winter.
Pay down what I owe without letting the Tally shame my household.
Keep Siv and Ake safe, and out of other people's quarrels.
sheet.mood: Wary, proud, and burdened by debt.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She can fend for herself better than most, but she is still my girl.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: son
relations.note: His feet carry him where his sense ought to stop him.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Her marks make a man feel smaller than his debt.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: I respect that he can bring meat home, but he likes a quarrel too much.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He pays in fish when he has them; I ask no foolish questions.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He knows the value of a hide and never forgets his own.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: Headwoman
relations.note: She keeps the town standing, though her word does not lighten my debt.

memories.gist: Last winter I counted what was left in the house and knew the fish would not stretch to spring. I took the trade I could get rather than watch my children go hungry.
At the last trade day, Maelis read my debt aloud. I stood there and let her finish, though I wanted to leave before she reached the sum.
Once I came back from checking traps and found Ake asking too many questions about a man he had seen in the woods. I told him some things were safer left alone.

stances.why: No council or tally will feel a child's hunger in my place.
A debt written down can grow heavier without putting food on the table.
I will deal with a man who brings fish, whatever town he calls home.
A feud would cost more than my household can afford.

sheet.secret: I privately trade hides and a bow with Rafe of Saltreach for smoked fish that he takes from the Storehouse. I know the fish is stolen, and keep the arrangement quiet.

sheet.narrative: I can put an arrow where I mean it, and I would rather be judged by that than by my father's debt. I hunt because I love the quiet before a shot and the proof of a clean hit. Eskil thinks every hunt is a contest; I let him think so if it keeps his eyes on me and not on my work.
goals: Keep improving my aim and earn respect as a hunter in my own right.
Help my family without letting our debts decide my worth.
Find out whether Jorund has the nerve to speak plainly to me.
sheet.mood: Steady and self-possessed, with a watchful edge.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: father
relations.note: He works hard for us, but he would rather swallow trouble than name it.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: brother
relations.note: I keep him close when I can; he thinks every rule is an invitation.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He is a good hunter when he remembers to watch the woods instead of me.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He watches me at the gate and hopes I do not notice.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: admirer
relations.note: She asks about my bow with the kind of attention that makes me smile.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He knows the hunt, but I do not like how quickly he turns every matter into a test of loyalty.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: fellow trapper
relations.note: She sees more than she says, and usually has good reason.

memories.gist: The first time I brought down a deer with a shot I chose myself, Father said nothing for a moment. Then he nodded, and that meant more than a speech.
At a hunt, Eskil rushed a shot and missed. I waited, took my time, and brought the animal down; he has remembered it ever since.
Liv watched me practice and asked if I would show her how to hold the bow. I let her try, though I warned her not to loose an arrow carelessly.
I caught Jorund looking my way when he had the gate watch. He turned back to his duty too quickly to pretend I had not seen.

stances.why: A clean shot feeds people; a loud claim does not.
The bow does not care who draws it.
I did not make the debt, and I will not let it name me.
Trade brings what our woods cannot, and a feud would make every journey dangerous.

sheet.narrative: I know how to make a fire, and I like to find out what is past the next hill or around the next tree. Siv says I should ask before I go, but asking usually means being told no. I like playing with Liv and Sten, and I am not afraid of the dark unless wolves are near.
goals: See more of the trade days without getting caught sneaking away.
Learn how traps work and how to make a good fire.
Keep playing with Liv and Sten.
sheet.mood: Restless and curious, with a little worry about wolves.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: father
relations.note: He gets quiet when I ask about the man I saw in the woods.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is good with a bow and tells me when I am being foolish.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She talks about hunting like it is the best thing there is.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We can find something to do even when the grown-ups are busy.

memories.gist: I went to a trade day even though I was meant to stay near home. There were baskets, fish, and strangers, and I thought I could watch without anyone noticing.
In the woods I saw Father meet a man from the south. I could not hear what they said, and Father looked stern when I asked him about it afterward.

towns.name: Saltreach
towns.character: an open fishing town on the southern shore, with reed beds, drying racks and a great storehouse where the Tally is kept: fishers, net-makers, basket-weavers, smokers, a healer and a scribe; fish and reeds are plentiful, timber and hides scarce
towns.ledger: The Tally of Saltreach, on the storehouse sign: Everything taken from the storehouse is told to the Tally-keeper and written. What is owed is paid before the next winter. Strangers are fed once and asked their business. No one goes north of the stone alone after dark.

buildings.name: the Tally House
buildings.about: The Tally is kept here and the Net-Council meets. The Written Code hangs by the door.

buildings.name: the Smokehouse
buildings.about: Fish are smoked here by Bea and her paid hands.

buildings.name: the Net-loft
buildings.about: Gwen's net-loft, where nets and baskets are made.

buildings.name: the Market
buildings.about: Goods change hands here for marks on market mornings, under the Market-warden.

buildings.name: the Trading House
buildings.about: Dunstan's trading house, where goods from the other towns are kept for sale.

sheet.narrative: I keep the Tally because a promise that cannot be read aloud can be bent by whoever has the loudest voice. I chair the Net-Council, issue marks against what the Storehouse holds, and know that my office gives me no power to command—only to make a decision valid by writing it down. Three times this season the smoked fish count has come up short, and I will not pretend the missing entries explain it.
goals: Find out why smoked fish is missing without accusing the wrong person.
Keep trade with Brandholm alive and press for debts to be settled through the Tally.
Teach Pim his letters and help him understand what a written promise is worth.
sheet.mood: Watchful and frustrated; steady in council, but uneasy about what the missing fish may mean.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He can make a room listen with a story, but I still check every storehouse count myself.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is bright enough to see more than she lets on.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: son
relations.note: His letters are slow work, but he is patient when it matters.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She is the only sane voice I hear from Brandholm, and I want her to learn our writing.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: council rival
relations.note: He thinks a badge can settle what a hearing and a record should settle.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She remembers what was sworn at the stone, and I trust her to say it plainly.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: council member
relations.note: He weighs his choices carefully; I wish he would choose a side before the winter.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: He counts everything, but he knows a broken trade costs more than a bad bargain.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: council member
relations.note: Her grief is real, though I fear it makes every Brandholm face look guilty.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: threat
relations.note: He fears no written debt and speaks of hunting across the middle lands as if the Oath were his to spend.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: storekeeper
relations.note: She keeps careful count for Brandholm; I wish more there understood that a tally is a safeguard, not a trick.

memories.gist: I read the Oath aloud at the stone again this midsummer, and heard both towns answer the same words without warmth but without refusal.
The third time this season, Corin and I found the smoked-fish store short of what the Tally said should be there. I checked the marks twice; the page still gave no answer.
I sat with Sigrun over a trade account and showed her how I set down a debt so neither side could quietly change its shape.
Orrin argued that Brandholm goods should be seized at market. I told him a seizure without a written judgment would make a thief of the Watch as well as the debtor.

stances.why: Both towns need what the other has, and I have seen how quickly old fear makes people call a neighbour an enemy.
A spoken account can be denied; a written one can be read aloud and challenged.
Taking goods by force would turn a debt into a grievance and risk the trade that keeps Saltreach warm.
The stores are short, but the Tally does not tell me who took anything or why.

sheet.narrative: I guard the Storehouse and hand nothing out unless Maelis has put it in the Tally. People say I tell the best stories in Saltreach; a good story can get a tired room to sit down before it starts shouting. I still miss the days I fished with Tomas, though I know better than to claim I understand what happened to him in the northern forest.
values: loyalty to family and old friends
goals: Keep the Storehouse sound through the next winter.
Stand by Maelis while she sorts out the missing fish and the argument over Brandholm's debts.
Keep the family talking to one another, even when council business follows us home.
sheet.mood: Easygoing on the surface, privately troubled by the missing stores and old grief.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the truth on the page; I keep the doors and bins from getting in her way.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has her mother's sharp eyes and a habit of keeping her thoughts to herself.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: son
relations.note: He asks questions as if every answer might open another door.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He knows the sea well and does not waste words when a net needs mending.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: council officer
relations.note: He has a hard job, but shouting does not make the numbers balance.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: widow of a friend
relations.note: I know what Tomas meant to her, and I do not try to tell her what to believe.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She can make both towns remember they once stood at the same stone.

memories.gist: Tomas and I pulled a net heavy with fish one grey morning, then argued over who had to gut them. We ate the smallest ones by the fire before we went home.
When Maelis first took charge of the Tally, I learned to wait for her mark before opening a store bin, even when I knew the household waiting outside.
I stood beside the Storehouse while Maelis counted the smoked fish again. The missing amount was not in the bins, and the Tally gave me no story to tell about it.
Anselm and I shared a meal after a rough fishing day and traded stories until the wind eased. He listened even when I had already told the ending once.

stances.why: If I make an exception without Maelis's record, no household can know the stores are being shared fairly.
People hear one another better after they have eaten and stopped bracing for a fight.
Saltreach needs northern timber and hides; Brandholm needs fish and smoked food.
Tomas was my friend, but I will not claim to know who killed him just because I miss him.

sheet.narrative: I work in Gwen's Net-loft, where a crooked knot can spoil a whole stretch of net, and I volunteer for the walks to Oathstone whenever there is room. I like the road, the lake, and the feeling that I can choose what to notice there. At home I keep some things to myself, even from people I love.
values: freedom to choose where I walk
goals: Become a net-maker whose work Gwen can trust without checking every knot.
Keep making the trade walks to Oathstone and see the people I care about there.
Find room for the life I want without turning my family or my work into a battleground.
sheet.mood: Bright and restless, with a private tenderness and a watchful edge.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices when a number is wrong; I hope she does not notice every other thing about me.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: father
relations.note: He makes the house feel easy, even when the grown-ups are worried.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: brother
relations.note: I like that he asks me to explain the letters he is learning.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: master
relations.note: She makes me redo a bad knot, but never pretends a good one was luck.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She knows when to ask a question and when to let me answer in my own time.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: beloved
relations.note: With her, the woods and the road feel like places I am allowed to want.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is far away in Brandholm, learning a trade that seems to suit his hands.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He carries messages quickly and makes the trade walks feel less lonely, though I hope he never asks too closely why I volunteer.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is bold and lively in the loft; I like her, even when she talks about visiting Pell as if Brandholm were simple to reach.

memories.gist: Gwen set a tangled length of net in front of me and made me undo every knot before I could start again. My fingers ached, but the next section held true.
On a walk to Oathstone, Runa and I found a quiet moment by the lake. I remember how carefully we listened for footsteps before we spoke honestly.
Elin noticed I was thinking about the next trade walk and asked if I wanted company. I changed the subject, and she let me.
Pim brought me a line of letters he had copied from Maelis. I helped him sound them out, and he was pleased when he read the last word by himself.

stances.why: A net that fails at sea costs more than the time it takes to learn the knot properly.
The road lets people meet as people, not only as the names their towns give them.
The person I love does not become less real because she was born across the stone.

sheet.secret: I am in love with Runa, Brann's daughter. I keep it private because our families and towns could make our affection into a quarrel.

sheet.narrative: I like the warmth of the fire and the scratch of Maelis's pen when she writes. I am learning letters, but some of them still turn around in my head. I want to see Brandholm's palisade and find out how tall it really is.
goals: Learn more letters from Maelis.
Go with the others to see Brandholm's palisade someday.
Play and talk with Robin and Rook.
sheet.mood: Curious and eager, with a little impatience for grown-up work.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She helps me with my letters and knows what each mark means.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: father
relations.note: He tells the stories I want to hear again.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She shows me things in the net-loft and never laughs when I ask.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We can talk about what we would look at in Brandholm.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is bolder than Robin and says we should really go.

memories.gist: Maelis showed me a word in the Tally and let me read it aloud twice. The second time I got it right.
Robin and Rook talked with me about the Brandholm palisade. We tried to guess how many people tall it was.

sheet.narrative: I make nets with my hands and keep my household standing with what the sea gives us. Tomas went north to trade and came back dead; Brandholm called it wolves, but I know a spear took him. I sit on the Net-Council, and I will not let his death be smoothed over for the sake of easy trade.
goals: Keep my net-house secure through winter.
Make Brandholm answer for what happened to Tomas.
Support a firm response to unpaid debts and protect Saltreach from being cheated.
sheet.mood: Grieving, resolute, and quick to anger when Brandholm is excused.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's stubbornness, and I fear what it will cost him.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She gives Tobin steadiness and Mira tenderness.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: I want her to grow up safe from the grief that shaped us.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She keeps her grief behind sharp words, and I do not always know how to reach her.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands what loss does to a household and does not ask me to forget.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He is right to press Brandholm, though his temper can make a bad bargain worse.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: councilwoman
relations.note: Her Tally is necessary, even when its cold marks cannot measure what we lost.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: His hunters are Brandholm to me, and I will not trust them near my family.

memories.gist: Tomas left for the northern forest to trade, and they brought his body back. Brandholm said wolves; I saw enough to know a spear had wounded him.
When Tobin first took a watchman's place, I saw how much of his father he carried in his face. I was proud and frightened at once.
Nell brought Mira into the world, and for a little while the house was full of the small sounds of a new life instead of old arguments.
Sabeth sat with me after another market day of talk about debts and Brandholm. She did not tell me to make peace with what happened.

stances.why: If I accept the wolves story, his death becomes nobody's responsibility.
Peace between towns matters, but it must not bury the dead.
Saltreach cannot keep lending food and goods without making the shares plain.
I want Mira and the others safe, though I have not learned how to set my own grief aside.

sheet.narrative: I serve under Orrin in the Watch, and I know how to fish, smoke a catch, and hold a spear. My father died in the northern forest, and Brandholm's answer has never satisfied me. I watch for the fish thief as ordered, but I have not stopped looking for the truth about Tomas.
goals: Learn what happened to Tomas in the forest.
