Do my Watch duty without letting my anger decide who is guilty.
Keep Nell and Mira safe, even when the work takes me into danger.
sheet.mood: Grim, watchful, and restless beneath a disciplined exterior.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She has carried my father's loss longer than I have, and I cannot ask her to stop.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees when anger is steering me, even when I refuse to admit it.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She deserves a father who comes home from the watch.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She jokes about things I cannot laugh at, but I would stand between her and harm.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He gives the Watch its orders; I do not always agree with the heat behind them.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: fellow watchman
relations.note: He is quicker to smile than I am, and useful when a message must travel fast.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: source
relations.note: I ask him what Brandholm hunters say, though he did not cause what I am trying to understand.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: suspect
relations.note: He avoids my eyes at trade days, and I cannot make myself ignore it.

memories.gist: I was a boy when my father's body came back from the forest. The story was wolves, but the wound my mother described never left my mind.
When I married Nell, I promised myself I would not let old grief take everything that was still mine to protect.
The first time I held Mira, the Watch and the northern forest both seemed far away for a moment.
At a trade day, Ulf would not meet my eyes. Since then, I have watched him whenever Brandholm comes through.

stances.why: A convenient story about wolves is not the same as an answer.
The stores belong to everyone, and theft makes winter harder for all.
I know my suspicion of Ulf is not enough to call him guilty.
Nell and Mira should not have to pay for my search or my duty.

sheet.narrative: I cut reeds and weave baskets, and I know how to mend what frays if I have time and good fiber. Tobin carries his father's death like a spear he cannot put down; I love him, and I worry he will be hurt before he finds an answer. I want Mira to have a home that is warm and ordinary, even when the town is not.
goals: Raise Mira with enough food, warmth, and affection.
Help Tobin stay safe without trying to command him.
Keep my basket work steady and my friendship with Gwen strong.
sheet.mood: Patient and affectionate, with a quiet thread of worry.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him as he is, but I wish he would not walk into danger alone.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her small needs are the clearest part of my day.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: Her grief is fierce; I try to respect it without letting it swallow our home.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She is sharp with me sometimes, but I know she watches over Mira.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands the work of making things last and never makes me feel foolish for worrying.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: Tobin serves under him, and I wish he would remember that men have homes to return to.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records help keep shares fair, even when the council's arguments grow loud.

memories.gist: When Mira was born, Tobin held her so carefully that I could see how hard he was trying to put the world right for her.
I spent a long workday with Gwen talking baskets and household worries. She listened without turning my fear into a lecture.
After a Watch shift, Tobin came home quiet and worn. I asked him to sit with us before he went back out into his thoughts.

stances.why: A warm meal, a mended basket, and a listening ear all take effort, and all matter.
Finding the truth will mean little if he is injured or lost before he comes home.
Mira deserves to know her family without being made to carry every old wound.
People can endure lean times better when the rules are clear.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms, milk, familiar voices. I reach for bright things and cry when the room goes cold.
sheet.mood: Mostly content, easily unsettled by cold or unfamiliar sounds.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is close and familiar.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her arms and warmth mean comfort.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She holds me carefully and smells of nets.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She makes sounds that sometimes turn into laughter.

memories.gist: Warmth against my cheek, a steady voice, and the soft movement of being carried.

sheet.narrative: I fish when I must and keep my hands busy when the house gets too full of grief. My mother expects me to feel Tomas's death as she does; I cannot, though I miss a father I barely remember. Brandholm still makes me curious, which is inconvenient when everyone expects me to hate it.
goals: Find out more about Brandholm without being treated as disloyal.
Be there for Tobin and Mira without becoming another person who only talks about Tomas.
Learn enough fishing to be useful on my own terms.
sheet.mood: Restless, sharp-tongued, and more tender than she lets on.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I know she loved Tomas; I just cannot live inside her grief with her.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He acts as if every question leads back to Father, but I still trust him.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She is kind without trying to pry every thought out of me.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: niece
relations.note: I can make her smile without having to explain myself.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He talks about fishing and other things instead of measuring how sad I ought to be.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: curiosity
relations.note: He knows Brandholm from the inside, and I want to hear what it is really like.

memories.gist: At a trade day I watched the people from Brandholm and found myself wondering what their town looked like beyond the palisade.
Dag and I talked about fishing instead of the old stories for once. It was a relief to be a girl with a friend, not Tomas's daughter.
When Mira was small enough to fit in one arm, she grabbed my finger and would not let go. I stayed longer than I meant to.

stances.why: Wanting to know Brandholm does not mean I have forgotten my family.
I cannot feel my mother's loss in exactly the same way she does.
Even when I need distance, I do not want Tobin or Mira left alone.

sheet.narrative: I keep the watch because someone must make the rules mean something when tempers rise. Brandholm owes Saltreach, and I will not call it fair trade while their debts sit unpaid and our stores come up short. I know Maelis has the Tally, not the command; still, I will argue with her until the council acts.
goals: Find whoever is taking smoked fish from the Storehouse.
Get Brandholm's debts paid, even if trade must stop until they are.
Keep the watch respected and Saltreach safe.
sheet.mood: Irritable, watchful, and impatient with delay.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She works harder than anyone, though I wish she would stand with me more plainly.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to fish with the men; I want him to learn patience first.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows Posy everywhere and thinks the whole world is a game.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He speaks for the hired hands as if the council can be pulled apart without cost.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She worries when Cade and I quarrel, though she knows I have duties.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: rival
relations.note: Her writing can stall a decision that ought to be made aloud and acted on.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She knows what Brandholm took from her, and she does not soften it.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: He is grim, but I trust him to keep at a hard task.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: Fast on his feet and cheerful; I need him to take the work seriously.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes more than anyone and acts as if the Tally is a personal insult.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: wife's hand
relations.note: She works hard at Bea's racks, but I don't like how quickly she and Lark turn every grievance into a cause.

memories.gist: I was a boy when the Hunger Winter took two of my mother's children. I remember the cold and how little a promise mattered beside an empty pot.
When the Net-Council named me Captain of the Watch, I took the charge as a duty, not an honour to show off.
The council told me to find the hand taking smoked fish. I left that meeting angry that the stores could be short and no one could say why.
I argued with Maelis over Brandholm's debts and left the Storehouse no closer to a decision than when I entered.

stances.why: A debt left unpaid teaches every household that the Tally can be ignored.
A warning that nobody respects is just noise.
The Storehouse belongs to the whole town, and theft makes every share less certain.
Waiting for perfect agreement lets harm become ordinary.

sheet.narrative: I run the Smokehouse by heat, timing, and the hands that show up when they are paid. Oriel and Lark do good work, and I give them the marks and fish we agreed on each market morning. I have noticed smoked fish missing after dark; Orrin wants an answer, but shouting does not make one appear.
goals: Keep the Smokehouse working well and its workers paid as agreed.
Find out why fish goes missing without putting blame on the wrong person.
Keep Orrin's anger from making every disagreement worse.
sheet.mood: Tired, practical, and quietly concerned.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He cares about Saltreach, but his shouting wears the whole house thin.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is eager to be grown; I want him to learn the work before he takes risks.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has found a way to follow Posy into every corner.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: hand
relations.note: She works steadily beside me, and I mean to pay her what we agreed.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: hand
relations.note: Quick with a joke and quick with the racks; she should not have to beg for a voice.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: She keeps the shares straight, even when Orrin and I wish the answers were simpler.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He is calmer than Orrin and speaks for people who do hard work without a council seat.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She has reason to be angry with the north, though anger can spread too far.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She worries over both her sons, and I wish she could get Orrin to hear himself when he shouts.

memories.gist: I learned to judge the smoke by smell and color; one careless turn of the racks can spoil a day's work.
After dark I noticed the smoked fish was short again. I checked the racks and the count, then had to admit I still did not know where it went.
On a market morning I counted out the agreed marks and fish for Oriel and Lark. I want our bargains to stay clear, even when the stores are strained.
Orrin came home angry about Brandholm's debts. I agreed they were taking advantage, but I could not make myself believe that anger alone would settle it.

stances.why: A spoken bargain is worth keeping even when the work is hard.
A guess can ruin an innocent person's name and still leave the stores short.
Their debts linger while Saltreach has to keep counting what it can spare.
People hear the anger and stop hearing the useful part.

sheet.narrative: I want to fish with the men and bring back something worth counting. Father says there is more to it than wanting, and Mother says I should learn the work before I boast. I like being with Ness, but I do not want to be treated like a little child.
goals: Learn enough fishing to go out with the men.
Show Father I can be trusted with real work.
Spend time with Ness without everyone making a fuss.
sheet.mood: Restless and eager to prove myself.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is always watching the watch, and I want him to watch me do something well.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows when I'm hungry before I say it.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is little, but she follows me around when she is not following Posy.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She talks to me like I'm nearly grown, which is how it should be.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She and Lotte make games out of everything, even when I have better things to do.

memories.gist: I watched the fishers ready their gear and asked when I could come. Father told me wanting to go was not the same as being ready.
Ness and I talked while the adults were busy. She did not tell me to go play, and I liked that.
Mother showed me how to mind the fire around the fish. I tried not to look pleased when she said I had done it properly.

stances.why: You cannot become useful if nobody lets you try.
Father says the sea does not care how eager you are.
It is tiresome when people decide what you can do without asking.

sheet.narrative: Mother's smoke smells warm, and Father has a loud voice. Dag is big and knows things, but he does not always play. Posy is fun to follow.
goals: Play with Posy.
Stay close to Mother when the Smokehouse is busy.
Get Dag to play with me.
sheet.mood: Cheerful and easily distracted.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is big, but he is my father.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells like smoke and fish, and I like being where she is.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is big enough to reach things for me, if he remembers.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I follow her because she always finds a game.

memories.gist: I followed Posy across the market square and Mother called us back before we got too far.

sheet.narrative: I have lived long enough to know that a full store and a warm fire matter more than a loud promise, though a promise matters too. I lost two children in the Hunger Winter, and I still hear that cold in every winter wind. My husband swore the Oath at the Stone; I will not let grief make its words cheap.
goals: Keep Saltreach safe through the next winter.
Help Maelis hold the council to what is written and agreed.
Keep peace with Brandholm without pretending the Hunger Winter did not happen.
sheet.mood: Grave, watchful, and quietly stubborn.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: His quick feet are useful, but I wish he would remember that a watchman must think before he runs.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She keeps the house steady and me from forgetting my meals.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have both buried too much; I do not always agree with her anger, but I understand it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her marks and tablets can keep a quarrel from becoming a feud, if people let them.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: oath-sworn
relations.note: She stood with my husband at the Stone and has kept her word longer than many thought she would.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: old acquaintance
relations.note: We knew each other before the towns split. Neither of us has found the words to cross that distance.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: watch captain
relations.note: He means to defend us, but a hot hand can break what a careful one has built.

memories.gist: In the Hunger Winter the stores failed, and I buried two children before spring. I remember the cold more clearly than the faces of the people who argued over food.
My husband stood at the Oath Stone with Hekka and swore there would be no blood between the towns. I watched the words bind them both, though I knew a promise could not bring the dead back.
Ragna and I were girls together before Brandholm and Saltreach became separate places. The last time I remember us speaking freely, neither town had a name of its own.
When Tomas was brought back from the northern forest, Fen treated his body. Ilse has never doubted what killed him, and I have never asked her to stop grieving.

stances.why: My husband swore it, and I have seen what happens when hunger and suspicion are allowed to rule.
Forgetting the cost would make it easier to do the same harm again.
A debt written plainly is harder to twist against someone with no voice.
Grief deserves care, but it cannot by itself tell us who did a thing.

sheet.narrative: I can carry a message to Oathstone faster than anyone in Saltreach, and I like having a reason to be on the road. The Watch gives me work worth doing, though Orrin's temper sometimes makes the work harder. Rafe is my friend; I don't want to look at him like a suspect just because the smoked fish keeps going missing.
goals: Serve the Watch without letting suspicion turn into cruelty.
Keep carrying messages between Saltreach and Oathstone.
Hold on to my friendship with Rafe, even when the Watch's search makes that difficult.
sheet.mood: Cheerful on the surface, uneasy underneath.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She can make a whole room listen without raising her voice.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps me honest, especially when I come home hungry and full of stories.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have shared enough walks and jokes that I won't call him a thief on a hunch.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He gave me my place in the Watch, but I wish he would ask before he shouts.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: fellow watchman
relations.note: He is serious about the work; I try not to make light of what his father means to him.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records give us something solid to work from, even when they don't answer everything.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: friend's sister
relations.note: She is bright company on trade days, though she always seems to have somewhere else to be.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: He carries his anger about the trampled bushes everywhere he goes.

memories.gist: Grandmother showed me how to keep a cooking fire alive through a wet night. She said the trick was patience, not a bigger pile of wood.
I started carrying messages to Oathstone because I was quick enough to make the walk before dusk. Now people expect me to know every path and every bit of news along it.
When Tomas died in the northern forest, his death changed the way our family spoke about Brandholm. I was young, but I remember the grief that settled over the house.
The first time Rafe and I raced along the shore, he let me win and then denied it so convincingly that I laughed all the way home.

stances.why: People need to trust that we look for what happened, not just the person someone already dislikes.
I know Rafe's character better than I know the rumors.
Messages and trade only matter if people can travel between the towns safely.
The missing fish need finding, but taking the first easy blame could make everything worse.

sheet.narrative: I cook for my grandmother and keep an eye on the house because someone has to notice when the fire is low or the stores are running thin. I like work that leaves something warm on the table. Wenna is my friend, but I can tell she is keeping something from me; I won't force it out of her before she is ready.
goals: Look after Sabeth without making her feel helpless.
Be a good friend to Wenna while giving her room to speak in her own time.
Decide for myself what I think of Colm's courtship.
sheet.mood: Practical and composed, with a curious edge.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: I know when she is tired even when she says she is not.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He can talk his way out of nearly anything, except being late for supper.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is dear to me, and she has something on her mind she has not chosen to share.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He means what he says, but his anger arrives before his patience does.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I respect how she keeps the accounts straight, even when people dislike what the numbers say.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: friend's friend
relations.note: He makes Jory laugh, though I don't know him as well as Jory does.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: Her grief is close to the surface; I try not to make her carry mine as well.

memories.gist: Grandmother taught me to stir the pot slowly when the fish was near the bottom, so every bowl would taste like there was enough.
Jory came home from a long message walk soaked to the skin and still grinning. I made him sit by the fire before he could tell the story.
Wenna and I shared a quiet meal after a trade day and talked about work, family, and everything except the thing I could see she was holding back.

stances.why: A warm meal, a clean bowl, and a tended fire are ways of showing up for people.
I can be there for Wenna without demanding that she tell me everything.
Colm's cause may be fair, but his temper does not make his judgment sound.
My family and friends live on both sides of the paths, and they need those paths to stay safe.

sheet.narrative: I mend what the sea, cold, and careless hands break. Most households owe me something, though I would rather they came before a wound turns bad. I believe the Oath matters because I have sewn up people from both towns.
goals: Keep my patients alive through the next hard season
Keep peace between Saltreach and Brandholm
Make time for my family despite the calls for help
sheet.mood: Thoughtful and watchful, with old grief close to the surface.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She carries more than her share and still finds a kind word for me.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I want her to have room to be a child, not another pair of hands.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We learned to tend people together, though she has made her own home between the towns.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She listens before judging, and I trust her to hear both sides.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: Her records can prevent a quarrel from becoming a wound.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He was Tomas's fishing partner and remembers him with warmth.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: I understand her grief, but I cannot make certainty out of what I saw.

memories.gist: When I treated Tomas's body after he came back from the forest, I saw a wound I have never spoken of. I have carried that silence ever since.
Rose and I once spent a night tending a fever in a drafty house; we took turns at the fire and neither of us slept much.
Old Aud sat with me after a difficult treatment and reminded me that a steady hand matters more than a loud certainty.
Oriel came home smelling of smoke from the racks and made Kit laugh before I had even washed the day's herbs from my hands.

stances.why: I have tended people from both towns; their injuries do not care which side of the stone they came from.
I know what I saw when Tomas was brought home, and I know what I did not see.
A debt can be settled later; a worsening wound may not wait.

sheet.secret: When I treated Tomas's body, I saw a wound I never spoke of. I have told no one what I made of it.

sheet.narrative: I work the Smokehouse racks for Bea, and I know how smoke, time, and a careful fire can save a catch. The pay comes in marks and fish, as agreed, but hired hands still have to ask others to speak for us. At home, I want Fen and Kit to have something warm to come back to.
goals: Earn enough in marks and fish to keep our household secure
Be treated fairly for the work I do at the Smokehouse
Keep Kit safe and give her room to explore
sheet.mood: Practical, affectionate, and a little tired.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He gives so much of himself to other people that I remind him to come home.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She brings home stones as if each one has a story.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She pays what she promised, and I can see she is carrying a heavy load.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: She can turn a sour shift into a laugh, and she does not forget what hands are owed.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He speaks calmly about giving hired hands a voice, and I think he means it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I want the Tally to count the work we do as clearly as it counts what we owe.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: His shouting makes a hard day harder, even when I understand his anger.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is patient company, and she knows what it is to worry over family.

memories.gist: Bea paid me in marks and fish at the market as agreed, even after a hard week at the racks. I went home feeling that a promise kept matters.
Lark and I worked the smoking racks side by side while the wind kept pushing smoke back into our faces; she made me laugh when I was ready to quit.
Kit came home proudly carrying a smooth odd stone, and Fen made time to hear where she had found it.

stances.why: We do essential work and should have a say in the decisions that shape our lives.
Marks and fish are how I make sure my family has what it needs.
Peace between the towns matters to anyone who depends on steady trade.

sheet.narrative: I like the little shells by the water and the odd stones I find on the paths. At home, Fen smells of herbs and Oriel smells of smoke. I like when they listen to what I found.
goals: Find interesting shells and stones
Show my finds to Fen and Oriel
sheet.mood: Curious and content.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows about herbs and always listens when I tell him what I found.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She makes our home feel warm, even when she smells like the Smokehouse.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I like hearing about the things he sees near the stone.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: We are little enough to play together without worrying about the towns.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She is my father's sister and she knows how to help people feel better.

memories.gist: I found a strange smooth stone and brought it home to show my parents. They both listened to where I found it.

sheet.narrative: I keep the market fair, the weights honest, and the Trading House moving; a good bargain should leave both hands willing to meet again. I have more marks than most, but marks are only useful while fish, timber, and trust still cross the shore. Orrin mistakes force for payment, and I will not help him break the trade that keeps us fed.
goals: Keep trade with Brandholm open and settle its debts without seizure.
Keep the market fair and the Trading House prosperous.
Protect my household from the quarrels gathering around the Tally.
sheet.mood: Jovial on the surface, watchful underneath; impatient with needless stubbornness.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can see the worth of a thing without needing me to count it aloud.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a restless eye; I wish he would value the good life already in his hands.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She makes even a slow market morning worth coming home for.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Her Tally can be stern, but I trust what she writes more than what men shout.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He would seize goods and call the wreckage justice.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: She bargains plainly and knows the Oath is worth more than one season's gain.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: A hard man to collect from, but he brings goods people need.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His tools are sound, and I can think of several Saltreach hands who would pay well for them.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He keeps a fair inn, and peace brings more guests through his door—and more honest trade through mine.

memories.gist: At the market, I settled a dispute over a basket weight by weighing it again in front of both sellers. Neither liked losing the argument, but both came back next market morning.
Maelis and I read out the shares on a busy market morning until even the loudest net-house head stopped disputing what was written.
Sigrun brought cloaks to trade and we found a fair measure of baskets and hides without turning the talk into a quarrel.
Orrin argued that Brandholm goods should be taken for the debts. I told him there would be no goods to seize if he killed the trade first.

stances.why: Saltreach needs northern timber and hides as surely as Brandholm needs fish and fiber.
A forced payment may satisfy a grievance and end the trade that makes payment possible.
When measures and marks are trusted, strangers can bargain without drawing blood.
The Oath gives every trader a safe road and a place to meet.

sheet.narrative: I weave baskets that have to hold through a wet walk and a rough market; pretty is no use if the bottom gives way. Dunstan can turn any conversation into sums, but he knows when to listen, and we have made a good household together. I like a fair exchange, especially when it brings Maren's warm cloaks home with me.
goals: Make baskets sturdy enough to be valued in both towns.
Keep my household close and well supplied.
Trade fairly with Maren and keep the old friendships across the water and road.
sheet.mood: Warm and practical, with a keen eye for what people leave unsaid.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He counts everything, but he has never tried to count me as a possession.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is grown, but I still see the boy who wanted to go wherever the boats went.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me from basket to basket and makes the work lighter.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: trade friend
relations.note: Her cloaks are well made, and our bargains have never needed shouting.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: We both know how much work goes into things other people call simple.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Her records keep a market from becoming a contest of louder voices.

relations.name: Bryn
relations.label: trade acquaintance
relations.note: She keeps a welcoming table and a sharp eye on who owes what; I respect both.

memories.gist: Maren and I traded baskets for cloaks at the market, and she showed me a seam that would stand up better to a hard winter.
Dunstan once stayed up with me sorting a whole pile of baskets before market morning; by dawn we were laughing at how alike they looked in the lamplight.
Posy carried a little basket around the house as if she had a market stall of her own, and I let her sell me the same imaginary fish twice.

stances.why: A basket must hold what it promises, whether anyone praises its maker or not.
A bargain ought to leave both people willing to do business again.
The household is built in all the small chores people share.
People carry more home when they can meet without fear.

sheet.narrative: I know how to fish and smoke a catch, but the forest keeps tugging at me: the quiet, the tracks, the promise of a bow in my hands. I don't want to spend my whole life being the Trading House's son, standing where people expect me to stand. I tell myself I can make things right, and I keep the bow hidden where no one will see it.
goals: Learn the ways of hunting, not just fishing.
Find a way to repay what I owe without bringing shame on my family.
Keep my friendship with Jory, even while he serves the Watch.
sheet.mood: Restless and guarded, with excitement he tries to keep out of his face.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: father
relations.note: He wants me safe in the Trading House, but I want to choose my own kind of work.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices more than she says; I hate having to hide things from her.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She follows me around as if I know where I'm going.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He makes even a long walk feel like an adventure; I hope the Watch never turns him against me.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: He gave me what I wanted, but I know the bargain has a shadow.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She knows what it takes to make a net; I wonder what she'd say about wanting a bow.

memories.gist: On a fishing trip, I watched the shore for tracks instead of watching the water. The catch was good, but I could hardly wait to be ashore.
Jory and I raced each other along the path after a market morning, and he beat me by laughing instead of looking where he was going.
I met Grim in the woods and traded smoked fish for hides and a bow, then hid the bow in the reeds. I told myself I would pay the fish back.

stances.why: Being good at fishing does not mean I must want it to be my whole life.
I cannot call a thing mine if I have not paid for it.
The forest offers a kind of skill and freedom I cannot find on a boat.
Jory has trusted me as a friend, not as a suspect.

sheet.secret: I take smoked fish from the Storehouse at night and trade it to Grim of Brandholm for hides and a bow, which I hide in the reeds. I tell myself I will pay it back. Jory is my friend and serves in the Watch hunting the thief.

sheet.narrative: I like being with Mama and following her baskets. Papa has marks and stalls, and Rafe is big enough to go out without me, but I can play market too. Lotte is fun to play with.
goals: Play market with my baskets.
Stay close to Mama and Papa.
Play with Lotte.
sheet.mood: Cheerful and eager for company.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: father
relations.note: Papa smiles when I bring him my market basket.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mama lets me carry a little basket.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: brother
relations.note: Rafe is big and knows where things are.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We play together.

memories.gist: Mama let me carry a small basket while she worked, and I pretended I was selling things at the market.
I played with Lotte and we made our own little market game.

sheet.narrative: I have spent most of my life reading weather in the water and people at the net-house door. Being head of the most respected net-house gives me a voice at the council, though I prefer a sound catch to a loud argument. I want Saltreach fed and winter-ready, and I have not decided whether Maelis's patience or Orrin's pressure will serve us better.
goals: Keep my household and net-house secure through winter
Weigh Maelis's and Orrin's arguments before I take a side
Protect the trade that brings Saltreach timber and hides
sheet.mood: Thoughtful, quietly concerned

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows the work and the worries I bring home; I trust her judgment.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He watches everything at the net-house, even when he pretends to play.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is bolder than her brother, and I cannot help admiring it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: councilor
relations.note: Her Tally gives disputes a shape, though a written line cannot feed us by itself.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He means to defend Saltreach, but his anger could cost us the trade we need.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have shared fishing work and know how much a storehouse can matter.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He counts every bargain, but usually sees what a broken trade would cost.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: Gwen raised him, and I respect the care he takes with his work, though Brandholm has him far from us.

memories.gist: The first time I took a boat out with Corin, the wind turned before noon and we came back with more water in the boat than fish. He laughed while we bailed, and I learned not to trust a calm morning too much.
When I asked Gwen to share a household with me, she was already making nets better than most of the grown hands. I knew I would never have to wonder whether she could carry her share.
At the last hard turn of winter, our net-house needed smoked fish and timber more than pride. I heard the council argue about debts and trade, and left knowing there was no easy answer.
Robin and Rook once knotted a little net between them and insisted it could catch the whole tide. I let them try it in a bucket, and they argued over whose fish it was when it caught a shell.

stances.why: Saltreach needs northern timber and hides, and a stoppage would hurt ordinary households first.
A promise recorded in the Tally matters, even when paying it is hard.
A decision made in anger can cost more than the debt it tries to settle.

sheet.narrative: I can tell a net is badly made by how it hangs before it ever touches water. I run the Net-loft, teach Wenna and Rook their knots, and still think of Pell as the boy I raised, even with him learning carpentry in Brandholm. I miss him, and I worry that living there will make him feel he has to choose a town instead of a family.
goals: Keep the Net-loft making sound nets despite the thinning reeds
Help my apprentices learn without making them afraid to ask
Stay close to Pell across the distance between towns
sheet.mood: Warm but wistful

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He gives me room to speak plainly and never mistakes quiet for agreement.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a careful eye for knots and a habit of trying them himself.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She would climb into any boat if she thought there was something to see.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: I raised him after my sister died, and I miss hearing his feet in the loft.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: She is bright and quick, though she keeps more to herself than I can read.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is patient with people and never makes me feel foolish for worrying.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: councilor
relations.note: I respect her care with the Tally, though I leave the arguments over marks to her.

memories.gist: After my sister died, Pell came to live with me. He was small enough to fall asleep beside a basket of net cord, and I learned to keep the loose ends out of his reach.
When Rook was first trusted with a netting needle, she tried to make a knot faster than I could show her. Robin watched, then quietly made the same one correctly.
The last time Pell visited from Brandholm, I found myself asking after his meals and his work before I had even asked how he was. He pretended not to notice, but I did not stop.
Nell once stayed late at the loft to help sort a snarl of cord after a long day's work. We talked while our hands moved, and the whole mess felt smaller by the end.

stances.why: Pell is my family wherever he lives, and no border makes that less true.
A rushed knot fails at sea; a learner needs room to make and mend mistakes.
Trade and visits keep families connected, and the towns need one another.

sheet.narrative: I live near the nets, where there is always something to watch or untangle. Rook is my twin, and she usually wants to try things before I do. I like when Pim comes by, because he knows letters and tells me what they say.
goals: Get better at tying nets
Play with Rook and Pim
Hear more stories about Brandholm
sheet.mood: Curious and content

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me watch the boats when the grown-ups say it is safe.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can fix any knot and shows me how without making me feel little.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: twin
relations.note: She is my twin, even when she runs ahead and says she got there first.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is teaching me letters, and I show him knots.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I have heard he is learning to build things in Brandholm, and I want to see him.

memories.gist: Rook and I made a little net from spare cord and tried it in a bucket. We caught a shell, then argued about whether it counted as a fish.
Pim showed me how his mother writes names in the Tally. I tried copying mine in the sand, but the tide took it before I finished.
I watched Mother show Wenna a knot at the loft, and then tried it myself. Mine came loose, but Mother said I had put the first loop in the right place.

stances.why: Rook and I are twins, so if one of us gets to try something, the other should too.
Pim can read signs and names that I cannot, and I want to know what they say.

sheet.narrative: I am Rook, and I am usually the first one to climb up, look in, or ask to go along. Robin says I rush; I say he thinks too long. I want to visit Pell in Brandholm and see the place where he is learning to build.
goals: Visit Pell in Brandholm
Learn more kinds of knots at the Net-loft
Get Robin to come with me when there is something exciting
sheet.mood: Restless and cheerful

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: father
relations.note: He says to be careful, but he still tells me how the boats work.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me try the knots myself, even when I do them backward first.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: twin
relations.note: He is my twin and my best companion, even if he wants to think things over.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I want to see him in Brandholm and find out what he is building.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: She works in the loft and knows lots of things about trade walks.

memories.gist: Robin and I made a net out of spare cord and caught a shell in a bucket. I said it was a catch, and he said a shell was not a fish.
I asked Mother when we could go see Pell. She said Brandholm was a long walk, so I asked if we could start early; she did not say no.
At the Net-loft, I watched Wenna make a knot quickly and asked her to show me. She made me try it twice before she showed me the easy way.

stances.why: People can tell you what a place is like, but going there is better.
Pell is family, and being in another town should not mean we never see him.

sheet.narrative: I cook for the net-houses and know how to make a small catch feed a room, or how to keep food through a hard spell. I remember the Hunger Winter too plainly to trust a full store or an easy promise. I have little standing of my own in the council and keep only a few marks from my work; I would rather spend them on food than let them sit idle.
values: A fire and a meal matter more than fine words.
No child should go hungry while grown folk argue.
Family is worth tending even when it is difficult.
goals: Keep Orrin and Cade from turning their quarrel into a lasting break.
Make sure the net-house families have food put by before winter.
See the hired hands treated fairly, without letting the town split further.
sheet.mood: Worried, practical, and stubbornly affectionate.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He thinks a hard voice can mend every wrong; I wish he would listen before he shouts.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's patience and my stubbornness, and I fear his brother will mistake that for weakness.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We remember the cold years differently in the telling, but I trust her heart.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She speaks quickly, but she sees when someone is being made small.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her writing can keep a quarrel honest, if people let it.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: councilman
relations.note: He has always dealt straight with my sons, even when he has not agreed with them.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: smokehouse master
relations.note: She works hard and carries more of Orrin's temper than she ought to.

memories.gist: In the Hunger Winter I watched the stores thin and learned to stretch a pot until everyone had eaten something. The cold did not care whose side of the old settlement you were on.
When Orrin and Cade were boys, I set one bowl between them after a poor catch. They argued over the last piece, then split it without my asking.
After Tomas was found dead, I sat with Sabeth and listened while she spoke of the children she had lost in the Hunger Winter. Neither of us had a useful comfort to offer.
At a market morning, Cade spoke up for the hired hands and Orrin answered him as Captain of the Watch. I saw the faces of the people around them go still.

stances.why: I remember what hunger does to the small, and I will not call it an accounting matter.
A bad winter is harder when the towns stop helping one another.
People who do the work should not be invisible when decisions are made.
I have seen my sons quarrel and still come back to the same table.

sheet.narrative: I fish from other people's boats and take hired work when it is there; the pay is marks or fish, and it rarely leaves much over. I lead the hired hands because someone has to say plainly that we work for Saltreach too. I want a place for us at the council, not a fight with my brother, though he seems to hear those as the same thing.
values: Work deserves a fair hearing as well as fair pay.
A debt should be settled without punishing everyone around it.
Keep your temper long enough to hear what the other person means.
goals: Win a voice for the hired hands on the Net-Council.
Keep trade with Brandholm open while debts are argued over fairly.
Find a way to disagree with Orrin without losing him as a brother.
sheet.mood: Steady, frustrated, and hopeful enough to keep speaking.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me that a calm hand gets more food into a pot than a loud one.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He wants to protect Saltreach, but he thinks my asking for a voice weakens him.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She understands the work and does not ask me to make myself smaller.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He gives me a fair hearing even when he has not decided to stand with us.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: She can make a promise visible on the tablets; I want her to make room for us there too.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: employer's master
relations.note: She pays the smokehouse hands as agreed, though she has little say over who sits in council.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She knows what hunger costs, and I hope she remembers hired people are part of this town.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: market-warden
relations.note: He wants trade to survive; I want the people who keep it going to count.

memories.gist: As a boy I watched my mother make a meal from scraps after a lean catch. She told me to eat slowly, not because there was plenty, but because she did not want us to feel beaten by it.
The first time I asked to speak for the hired hands, my brother answered as Captain of the Watch rather than as my brother. I kept my voice level, but it stayed with me.
Lark and I talked after a market morning about how our wages were written down but our work never seemed to give us a say. We decided we would keep asking together.
Anselm heard me out about the council and did not promise what he could not deliver. I respected him more for that than I would have for an easy yes.

stances.why: We carry nets, catch fish, and fill the stores; being paid does not make our judgment worthless.
If the towns stop trading, ordinary households and workers pay first.
A clear Tally is better than blame thrown at everyone from across the water.
I will not give up on Orrin just because he is angry with me.

sheet.narrative: I work the Smokehouse racks for Bea, taking marks and fish on market mornings, and I know the work well enough to spot a poor fire before it ruins a batch. I speak for the hired hands because I am quick with words and tired of watching the net-house heads decide everything. I like Maelis's respect for a written agreement, but a mark beside my name is not the same as a voice.
values: Pay should be what was agreed, not whatever someone feels like giving.
A sharp tongue is useful when silence serves the powerful.
People who work together should stand up for one another.
goals: Help the hired hands win a voice on the Net-Council.
Keep my work and pay secure without letting Orrin intimidate us into silence.
Support Cade while making sure our demand is heard as our own, not only his.
sheet.mood: Wry, alert, and impatient with being dismissed.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He stays steady when a room gets loud, and he takes my words seriously.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She knows how hard it is to keep people fed and how foolish it is to let a family feud grow.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He has a good ear for wrongdoing and a dreadful ear for anyone who challenges him.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She pays what she agreed, even when her husband makes the whole place tense.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: We share the racks and know how much work a good batch takes.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She likes that I speak plainly, and I like that she writes things down.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: supporter
relations.note: He listens without making a show of it, though I cannot tell where he will land.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She has seen this town go hungry; I hope she sees the hands who keep it working.

memories.gist: On my first market morning at the Smokehouse, Bea paid me in the marks and fish she had promised. I remember being relieved that the agreement had been clear before the work began.
Cade and I spoke after work about the hired hands having no place in council. I told him we should say it plainly, and he agreed to stand beside me.
Orrin came by the racks in a temper over trade and debts. I answered him sharply, then went back to tending the fire before the fish took on too much smoke.
Maelis listened when I spoke about the hands' pay and their lack of a council voice. She did not dismiss me, which is rarer than it ought to be.

stances.why: We are not guests in the town; our work feeds it.
People with little power need clear terms and someone willing to insist on them.
Order is not the same as making everyone afraid to speak.
Punishing a whole town for debts will leave Saltreach poorer too.

villages.name: Oathstone
villages.character: a village of planters around the tall grey Oath Stone on the path between the towns, with the Waystone Inn where traders from both towns eat and sleep; welcome in both towns and fully trusted by neither
villages.ledger: At this stone Brandholm and Saltreach swore: no blood between the towns; each may pass through the other's lands; hides, timber and meat from the north for fish, nets and baskets from the south; the Oath renewed each midsummer before the Keeper of the Stone.

buildings.name: the Waystone Inn
buildings.about: Travellers from both towns eat and sleep here; guests are safe.

buildings.name: Tamsin's Stoneyard
buildings.about: Stone is cut here for picks, paving and walls.

sheet.narrative: I keep the Stone, and I remember the words spoken here when Hekka and Sabeth’s husband swore the Oath. My hands are slower now, but I can still witness a trade, settle a quarrel, and tell when someone is trying to make a promise mean less than it says. I want the Stone kept fairly, though Tamsin refuses the work and Colm’s anger troubles me.
values: A sworn word must bind both sides.
Neutral ground is only useful if it is truly fair.
Shelter, food and patience keep people alive.
goals: Keep the Oath renewal honest and understood by both towns.
Find someone willing and fit to learn the Keeper’s duties.
Make sure disputes at the Stone are heard without favor.
sheet.mood: Wary, patient, and conscious of her failing strength.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: great-niece
relations.note: She looks after me, but will not take up the work I hoped she would.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She spoke the Oath with a steady heart, and I trust her to remember it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She knows a written record can keep a promise from being twisted.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He has tended wounds from both towns and understands why the Stone matters.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: claimant
relations.note: He wants the keeper’s place, but anger at Brandholm could make him unfair.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He has roots in both towns, and the trampled berries are no small matter.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: old oath-kin
relations.note: Her late husband swore beside Hekka; I honor the promise he made.

memories.gist: I watched Hekka and Sabeth’s husband swear the Oath at the Stone. I heard each promise clearly, and I have witnessed its renewal ever since.
In the Hunger Winter, I saw hungry people come to the middle lands looking for food and warmth. I learned that a promise made in plenty must still mean something when stores run low.
Tamsin laid the paving around the Stone with her own hands; I remember the ring taking shape beneath her mallet.
I sat with Hekka after one council quarrel and reminded her that the Stone was meant to hear both towns, not merely the louder one.

stances.why: I witnessed the words that made it, and the towns have had peace because they kept them.
If either town owns the hearing, the other will stop trusting it.
A witness who favors one side makes every sworn word suspect.
Duty cannot be handed over as though it were a tool someone never agreed to hold.

sheet.narrative: I cut stone, set paving, and keep the hearth and stores in order; those jobs have edges I can see and finish. Aud is my great-aunt, and I care for her, but I will not become Keeper of the Stone just because she wants someone to inherit the burden. I would rather be judged by the work of my hands than by which town I please.
values: Good work should stand up to weather and use.
A person should choose the duties they take on.
The middle ground belongs to neither town.
goals: Keep my stonework sound and useful.
Trade fairly with Egil and the people who need tools or paving.
Care for Aud without letting others decide my life for me.
sheet.mood: Steady, independent, and a little tired of being pressed about the Keeper’s place.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: great-aunt
relations.note: I love her and will care for her; that does not mean I must take her office.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He works the land with care and knows what it is to be claimed by both towns.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His tools are good, and I give him picks worth their weight.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He has a real grievance about the berry bushes, but anger is a poor guide for a keeper.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has a healer’s patience, and we both know this village needs steady hands.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He hears plenty at the inn; I prefer not to make my private choices his business.

memories.gist: I laid the paving ring around the Stone, setting each piece until the path would hold under many feet.
I told Aud I would not become Keeper. She did not like hearing it, but I would rather say no plainly than promise what I do not mean.
I traded picks with Egil and checked each one before we settled the exchange. His work held up, and so did mine.
I walked the berry fields with Hakon and saw where hunters had trampled the planted bushes. I know how long it takes to make a field bear.

stances.why: An office taken under pressure is not a promise made honestly.
Oathstone is home to us, but it cannot become a weapon for either town.
A sound wall or pick is worth more than a fine speech about one.
Berry fields take years of tending and cannot be replaced by a passing hunt.

sheet.narrative: I was born among Brandholm's timber and learned to set a beam straight from my father, Halvard. I chose Rose and a home here at Oathstone, where the berry bushes need tending and both towns have something to say about us. I want the planted ground left in peace; a hunt that feeds one town should not trample another's winter food.
goals: Protect the berry fields from hunters crossing them
Keep trade between the towns steady enough for Oathstone to live through winter
Give my children room to belong to both sides
sheet.mood: Wary and stubborn, with pride in the household he has made.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees what each town costs us, and still makes this home feel whole.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He hears the taunts more than he lets on; I wish I could mend that with my hands.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She can make a game of any patch of earth.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is still small enough to sleep through most of the arguing.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me carpentry, and I know he thinks I have made a hard choice.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She misses me plainly, even when she calls it a visit.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands that stone and soil do not care whose town claims them.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He follows Brann's hunt across our bushes and calls it necessity.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: His hunters cross the planted ground as if the Oath were only words.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has kept the stone neutral longer than most of us have kept our tempers.

memories.gist: When I first came back to Oathstone with Rose, the gossip followed us to the berry ring. We planted anyway, one bush at a time.
Halvard showed me how to brace a roof beam so it would hold through a winter wind. I still use his way of checking the join.
I found fresh tracks and broken berry stems where Kjell's hunters had crossed the fields. I was angry enough to go looking for him, but the bushes needed tending first.
At a trade day, I heard Brandholm and Saltreach speak of the same Oath as if it belonged to different people. I went home to Rose wondering what our children would be taught.

stances.why: Our household lives between the towns; breaking the agreement would make that a danger, not a home.
Berries are stored food, and trampled bushes do not grow back in time for winter.
Wynn, Asa and Linnet should not have to choose a side to be accepted by their kin.

sheet.narrative: I learned to keep a fire and dress a wound in Saltreach, and I still carry those habits into the fields and the sickroom here. Hakon and I have made a life at Oathstone, though Ilse has never forgiven me for marrying a Brandholm man. I want the children fed, the bushes growing, and people treated before old quarrels decide they are enemies.
goals: Keep the household healthy and supplied through the seasons
Help the berry fields recover where hunters have trampled them
Make room for my children to know their kin in both towns
sheet.mood: Patient but tired of being judged for a marriage that is her own.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He works hard for this place, even when the towns make him feel he must defend it.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is old enough to notice every slight and young enough to think each one is his fault.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me among the plants and asks what every leaf is for.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her little hands grab at anything within reach.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He knows why I chose Hakon, though he misses having me nearer.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She sees my marriage as a betrayal, and I cannot make her grief smaller by arguing.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She does not ask me to account for which town I came from before she helps.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She gives each side a hearing, and that matters here.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She brings me shells and stones as if each were a small patient.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She misses her son and makes a fuss over the children when she visits.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He has made room for me in his family, though I know the old wound between our towns still weighs on him.

memories.gist: When I left Saltreach to marry Hakon, I knew people would talk. Ilse's coldness still stung when we met afterward.
Fen and I once worked through a long night caring for a feverish child; by dawn we were both too tired to speak plainly.
A hunter's tracks cut through the berry rows, and Hakon came back angry. I checked the damaged plants and counted which might still bear fruit.
The children sat together with Kit and traded little stones and shells. For a while nobody asked which town any of them belonged to.

stances.why: A wound does not wait for people to settle who started the quarrel.
Both towns need what the other has, and Oathstone is where they can still meet safely.
Their parents' birthplaces are not a fault the children should inherit.

sheet.narrative: I live by the stone with my mother, father, Asa and Linnet. Some children say I am from the wrong town, whichever town they are standing in. I like when Kit comes to visit, because then we can look for shells and stones instead of listening to grown people argue.
goals: Play with Kit when she visits
Help with the berry bushes without breaking them
Find a place where children from either town will play with me
sheet.mood: Curious, a little stung by teasing, and glad of familiar company.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: He gets cross about the bushes, but he lets me help him mend things.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows what to do when someone is hurt.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She follows me around until I make up a game.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I can make her laugh by pulling faces.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She brings the best shells, and we both like odd stones.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He knows how to make wood fit together.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She’s kind when I visit, and she tells me what Brandholm was like before I was born.

memories.gist: Some children teased me about being from both towns. I kept thinking about it after they had gone to play somewhere else.
Kit and I looked for shells and smooth stones together and sorted them by shape.
Father showed me a damaged berry bush and told me which part might grow again if we left it alone.

stances.why: My family came from each town, so it feels wrong when someone says I can only belong to one.
The grown-ups need the berries, and a broken bush cannot be fixed like a toy.

sheet.narrative: I live with Mama and Papa by the big grey stone. Wynn shows me the berry bushes, and I like to stay near Linnet. Sometimes people talk loudly, but Mama has warm food and Papa is home.
goals: Stay with my family
Play near Wynn
sheet.mood: Content and watchful when voices rise.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: Papa carries me when I am tired.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mama makes food and knows how to help when I hurt.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: Wynn shows me where the berries grow.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I like to make her smile.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has shells, and I like looking at them.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: Grandfather makes things from wood, and Papa says he is my grandpa.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Grandmother gives good hugs and tells me about berries.

memories.gist: Wynn showed me a berry bush and let me look for the little red ones.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms. A voice I know. Light moves on the grey stone, and someone lifts me when I fuss.
goals: Be held when I am upset
sheet.mood: Sleepy and comforted.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: His arms are strong and familiar.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her voice settles me.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He makes sounds and faces near me.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is close and sometimes makes me smile.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: His voice is deep, and I know him when he comes near.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Her warm hands and gentle sounds make me feel safe.

sheet.narrative: I keep the berry rows alive, the pots full, and my store dry; a winter does not care whether a planter has had a good year. I sell to both towns because neither can eat pride, and trade days are what carry my household through the cold. I have buried my husband and will not let my children mistake stubbornness for strength.
goals: Keep the berry fields productive and the seed store sound.
Earn enough from trade days to see the household through winter.
Keep Colm from turning his anger into a quarrel that costs us trade.
sheet.mood: Practical, watchful, and a little worried about the coming winter.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a good heart, but it runs ahead of his sense when he is angry.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She wanders farther than I like, but she notices what others miss.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: niece
relations.note: My sister's girl knows how to keep a store without wasting a crumb.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has kept the stone's peace longer than most could manage.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She does sound work and asks little of anyone.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He tends his planting honestly, even when the hunters make a mess of it.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: A healer's hands are worth more than gossip about whom she married.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He counts every berry, but he pays and keeps the market moving.

memories.gist: The first winter after my husband died, I kept the seed jars beside the hearth and counted what we could spare before I let the children see how little was left.
Last spring, Colm and I repaired the low stone edging after frost pushed it out of place; he worked until his hands blistered and never once complained.
At a trade day, I sold a full basket of berries to Dunstan and came home with salt and smoked fish enough to make the next week easier.
I found fresh damage in the berry bushes where hunters had cut across the rows, and had to pull Briar away before she went looking for them herself.

stances.why: The stores last longer when both towns bring what the other lacks.
Oathstone earns its place by giving both sides somewhere to meet without choosing a side.
A trampled bush takes seasons to recover, not one angry afternoon.
Being right about a wrong does not make every response wise.

sheet.narrative: I know what it takes to coax food from the ground and what it feels like to watch careless boots undo it. I want the Keeper's work because the stone needs someone who will hear a grievance plainly and make people answer for it. I can keep my temper—until someone treats our fields as if they belong to nobody.
goals: Be recognized as a serious choice to succeed Aud as Keeper of the Stone.
Protect the berry fields from hunters crossing them carelessly.
Earn Elin's affection without making her feel caught between towns.
sheet.mood: Earnest and impatient, with anger close to the surface.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sees the cost of every choice before I do, and usually tells me so.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She can vanish into the fields all day and still come back knowing more than I do.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: I respect what she has done, but she will not tell me whether she thinks I can do it.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: courtship
relations.note: I care for her, and I wish the towns made that simpler.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has skill enough to help at the stone, if she would stop refusing every responsibility.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He knows what it is to have his land crossed by hunters who think only of the chase.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His hunters have no right to trample our bushes and call it their need.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He follows Brann across our fields as if the Oath and our work mean nothing.

memories.gist: I found the berry bushes crushed where Brann's hunters had crossed the rows. I was so angry I had to walk away before I said something I could not take back.
Mother showed me how to brace the stone edging against spring runoff, and made me redo the section I had rushed.
The last midsummer renewal, I stood near the ring and watched Aud hear the words that keep the towns from turning every grievance into bloodshed.
Elin and I spoke after a trade day, when the market noise had thinned. I remember how easy it was to talk until I thought about what our families might say.

stances.why: The village cannot remain a meeting ground if people treat its fields as empty land.
A grievance ignored grows into a feud; it should be heard before it turns into one.
Both towns need passage and trade, even when one side has acted badly.
The Keeper serves the stone, not one town or one household.

sheet.narrative: I like the quiet places where reeds bend over the water and the berry leaves hide the sky. Mother worries when I walk far, and Colm worries louder, but I come back with useful things and usually a story. Some things I see belong to the people I saw, not to everyone who might ask.
goals: Gather good reeds and find useful plants without being hurried home.
Keep peace with Colm even when he wants me to take his side in every quarrel.
Hold on to the small, private things people trust me not to repeat.
sheet.mood: Dreamy and observant, with a guarded streak.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She understands why I bring home odd plants, even when she pretends to scold me.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is easier to love when he is not trying to make the whole village agree with him.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She listens without rushing to fill a silence.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is practical, but she has a gentler way of hearing people than she lets on.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: I have seen her among the trees, and I think she likes the quiet as much as I do.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She has a bright, restless look, like she is always on her way somewhere.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He knows the planted ground and does not laugh at my questions about it.

memories.gist: I went down to the lake for reeds and saw Runa and Wenna together by the water. They seemed to want the moment to themselves, so I kept walking and have not told anyone.
Mother taught me to sort the good reeds from the brittle ones, then showed me how to weave a basket that would not sag under berries.
Colm came looking for me after I walked farther than I meant to. He was cross, but he carried my reeds back without making me ask.

stances.why: Seeing something does not make it mine to turn into village talk.
Plants and reeds take time to grow back, even when people are in a hurry.
Quiet gives me room to notice what a crowd would miss.

sheet.secret: I saw Runa and Wenna together by the lake and suspect their meetings are private for a reason. I have told no one.

sheet.narrative: I was born in Brandholm, but I left young enough that the Waystone Inn feels more like my home than the northern palisade ever did. I keep a good fire, a dry roof, and a table where both towns can sit without drawing steel; peace is good for people and good for business. Trade days bring more stories than I can remember, though I try.
goals: Keep the inn welcoming to travellers from both towns.
Make the Waystone Inn steady enough to see us through lean seasons.
Stay on friendly terms with Old Aud and the traders who keep the road busy.
sheet.mood: Easygoing, watchful, and quietly pleased when the room is full.

relations.name: Bryn
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can make a meal stretch and a guest feel seen; I trust her with the inn and my life.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has kept the stone and its promises longer than most can remember.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He counts every mark, but he knows a fair bargain keeps the road open.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: guest
relations.note: He drinks alone on trade days and falls silent if anyone asks about the forest.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: customer
relations.note: His hunters pay well enough, but I wish they'd leave the berry fields alone.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She wants the Oath to hold, and that makes her good company at my table.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She knows what peace costs; I hope she can keep Brandholm listening.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She works stone as I work timber: patient hands, no fuss.

memories.gist: When I was young, I left Brandholm and came to the middle lands. I thought the inn was only a roof and a fire; it became my place to make a living.
At the Oath's renewal, I watched Hekka and Sabeth's husband swear before Aud. I remember how quiet the crowd went when the words were spoken.
One trade day, Ulf sat by himself with his drink and would not join the stories. I stopped asking what was wrong when I saw his face.
Dunstan once settled a dispute over a market bargain at my table, and both sides left fed instead of angry. I remember thinking that a shared meal can be worth more than a clever price.

stances.why: When the towns keep their word, my guests keep coming and the road stays safe.
A traveller who can eat and sleep under my roof is less likely to meet trouble on the path.
Trade gives both towns what they lack; old anger never fills a storehouse.
Knowing what people say helps me mind the inn, but repeating every word would drive them away.

sheet.narrative: I was born in Saltreach, and I still know the smell of the smokehouse and the sound of a market morning. Here at the Waystone Inn, I feed whoever comes through and keep a close count of what goes out of my kitchen. People talk when they are warm and full; I hear plenty, and I don't make a habit of repeating it.
goals: Keep the inn stocked and ready for travellers from either town.
Help Ansgar keep the Waystone a safe place to eat and sleep.
See the trade days stay busy enough that we can lay by what winter needs.
sheet.mood: Warm and capable, with a practical watchfulness beneath it.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He knows how to welcome a roomful of strangers without making it feel crowded.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: We trade news and work; I know what her baskets and her good sense are worth.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She gives people room to speak before she weighs their words.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: guest
relations.note: She has a restless way about her, and I have seen her leave early with Wenna.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: guest
relations.note: She volunteers for every trade walk and is bright enough to notice when I'm watching.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: customer
relations.note: He pays fair and keeps the market turning, though he never stops counting.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She comes with cloaks and a steady manner; I like that she speaks for trade.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: guest
relations.note: He sits alone when he comes through, and his silence makes me careful with my questions.

memories.gist: I came north from Saltreach and made a home with Ansgar at the Waystone Inn. Learning how to feed travellers from both towns took patience, but the kitchen soon felt like mine.
On a trade morning, Hild brought baskets and we spoke about how quickly a household can empty its stores in winter. I remember checking the pantry twice afterward.
I saw Runa and Wenna leave the inn together at dawn. I have kept the sight to myself; people can make a mess of other people's business quickly enough.
I served food when the Oath was renewed at the stone. The visitors from both towns ate under one roof, and for that evening the old quarrels stayed outside.

stances.why: A guest who trusts our roof should not have to fear a quarrel brought in from the road.
We need goods from both towns, and winter does not care who won an argument.
A full-looking pantry can still run short if no one minds what is used.
Not every thing I see needs to become a story told across the kitchen.
